title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
summary: This research explores how intrinsic motivation, similar to human curiosity and creativity, can be leveraged to build robust world models in AI systems, particularly in the absence of external rewards or task supervision. It investigates fundamental aspects of AI intelligence development.

title: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems
summary: This paper introduces an architecture for cognitive memory reconstruction in language model systems using activation-guided graph retrieval, proposing that long-lived AI systems require activation-conditioned memory availability in addition to query-conditioned relevance. It focuses on how AI systems store and recall information.

title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
summary: This research investigates the measurement limits of LLM reasoning failure taxonomies, demonstrating that reported fractions of errors in specific categories are often properties of the measurement process itself, rather than solely reflecting model performance. It critiques current evaluation methods for LLM reasoning.

title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
summary: This paper explores "student-aware skill transfer" for LLM agents, investigating whether a stronger LLM can more effectively teach a student LLM agent by reasoning about the student's latent state, similar to Theory of Mind. It focuses on the learning and interaction of AI agents.

title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
summary: This research introduces a cognitive multi-agent system for search and rescue operations, focusing on language-grounded hierarchical reinforcement learning to enable coordination among multiple heterogeneous agents. It addresses challenges in autonomous system collaboration for critical missions.

title: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient
summary: This paper argues that AI alignment, defined as ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human values, is neither solvable nor sufficient to guarantee beneficial AI outcomes and avoid societal harm. It contributes to the broader philosophical debate surrounding AI ethics.

title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
summary: This research introduces a framework for creating composable agentic workflows by combining BPMN, LLM-based agents, and enterprise knowledge, aiming to improve the coordination, understanding, and monitoring of complex agentic applications. It focuses on orchestrating AI agents in workflows.

title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
summary: This study examines AI-assisted measurement of administrative texts, specifically US tax filings, addressing challenges arising from human disagreement in text labelling and focusing on dollar-weighted measurement and selective machine labelling with budgeted human review. It presents a real-world application of AI.

title: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
summary: This study evaluates the reliability of Claude Code, an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 large language model, when used as a grading system for handwritten university exams. It assesses its agreement with expert human grading.

title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
summary: This paper introduces W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime designed for executing weight-space intervention programs on pretrained language models, enabling parameter updates, projections, and transformations. It offers a new method for deep-level model manipulation.

title: Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning
summary: This research investigates the application of large language models (LLMs) for clinical decision support and medical reasoning, using medical multiple-choice questions as a testbed to evaluate their capability to discriminate between plausible options. It explores AI's role in medical diagnostics.

title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
summary: This paper introduces the Neural Control Plane (NCP), a closed-loop system that observes language model execution, synthesizes, and evaluates weight-space intervention rules to optimize control policies. NCP separates the inference data plane from the control plane for pretrained models.

title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
summary: ExpertCrowd-SWE is introduced as a new benchmark comprising 100 expert-authored software engineering tasks designed to evaluate the performance of frontier autonomous coding agents in complex, unfamiliar codebases. It provides a rigorous evaluation method for AI coding capabilities.

title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
summary: This empirical study focuses on the dependability of long-horizon LLM agents by conducting a trajectory-centered analysis to identify where errors originate and how control mechanisms address them during complex tasks. It aims to improve the reliability of AI agents.

title: Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent
summary: This research explores scalable network-based interventions for HIV treatment and prevention using the R2C-Agent, aiming to optimize the targeting of limited public health resources. It demonstrates an AI agent's application in public health challenges.

title: F3-AGI v4.0: Bioenergetically-Gated Active Inference, Metaplastic Preconditioning, and Residual Program Synthesis for Sample-Efficient Abstract Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces F3-AGI v4.0, a system employing bioenergetically-gated active inference, metaplastic preconditioning, and residual program synthesis for sample-efficient abstract reasoning in few-shot learning scenarios like ARC-AGI. It addresses challenges in inducing algorithmic transformations from limited demonstrations.

title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
summary: This research explores agent-guided discovery of exchange-correlation functionals using language-model agents and symbolic search, with physics-based validation, for predictive density functional theory. It investigates the efficacy of AI agents in scientific discovery.

title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
summary: This paper proposes an epidemiologic cohort design to study the long-term behavior development and outcome influence of AI agents, particularly as they increasingly perform autonomous tasks across various sectors. It suggests a methodological approach for understanding agentic AI.

title: Disentangling Multimodal Rotary Positional Embedding in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research introduces a method for disentangling Multimodal Rotary Positional Embedding (MRoPE) in vision-language models, which encodes spatial structures for visual and text tokens.

title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
summary: This paper proposes MPIUR, a technique for multimodal recommendation that integrates textual item descriptions, images, and user reviews within a unified framework for e-commerce platforms.

title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
summary: This paper presents an impossibility theorem demonstrating that no finite rulebook can certify every safe program, highlighting fundamental limitations in gatekeeping AI agents based solely on code.

title: Online-Adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Neuro-symbolic Financial Forecasting
summary: This research introduces a neuro-symbolic framework combining online-adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps with LSTM networks for financial forecasting, designed to handle market regime shifts and nonlinear dynamics.

title: Living constitutions: Participatory alignment for sovereign foundation models
summary: This paper explores participatory alignment for 'Constitutional AI' and foundation models, addressing the challenges of how values are encoded and governed in AI through a plain-text 'constitution'.

title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
summary: SteerDistill is a new technique for quantizing LLM agents to reduce inference costs while maintaining task success by using closed-loop teacher steering to guide quantized agents.

title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
summary: SafeRoute-MAS is a coverage-aware and risk-calibrated message routing procedure introduced for multi-agent systems performing scientific reasoning, aiming to improve performance by selectively handling specialist messages.

title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
summary: This study investigates how Chain-of-Thought reasoning in generative AI models can foster anthropomorphism, perceptions of epistemic superiority, and cognitive deference in human users.

title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
summary: WoW (World Knowledge) is proposed as a new large-scale world knowledge corpus designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models, addressing the fragmented nature of existing Chinese educational datasets.

title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
summary: This research focuses on data preparation and adaptation of the SraVaani speech foundation model for Nepali-English code-mixed speech recognition, aiming to improve performance on language-switched utterances.

title: Agent Benchmarks Stop Ranking Before They Run Out of Tasks
summary: This paper discusses the limitations of existing benchmarks for data-science and ML-engineering agents, highlighting that they often stop differentiating top models before running out of tasks.

title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration
summary: Darmok is introduced as an automated system that achieves superhuman performance in solving British cryptic crosswords through constraint tightening and resilient orchestration.

title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
summary: This paper presents an ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case, addressing the non-uniqueness and ambiguity in geological modeling.

title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
summary: This research proposes 'Predictive Surprise' as a self-grounding concept bottleneck for creating interpretable time-series classifiers that are accurate, interpretable, and capable of abstaining when evidence is weak.

title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
summary: ADIndex is a new method for layer-adaptive sparse attention indexing via group-level distillation, designed to reduce latency in long-context inference for models using DeepSeek Sparse Attention.

title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
summary: This paper explores how reward diversity can be a benefit, rather than a hurdle, in personalized federated reinforcement learning, challenging traditional views on collaboration in multi-agent systems with distinct goals.

title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
summary: StatPrompt-LLM introduces a lightweight statistical refinement method for foundation-style models in time-series forecasting, designed to better expose fundamental temporal structures.

title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
summary: MADSNet is a new Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network developed for spike camera image reconstruction, designed to efficiently process high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams.

title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Third Eye explores the long-term utility of recursive self-improvement in AI models, investigating whether self-updates remain useful after subsequent model updates, evaluating various backbones on math and code.

title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers
summary: This survey provides an overview of models, benchmarks, and frontiers in multimodal graph learning, where nodes carry diverse modalities like text and images, and edges encode relations among entities.

title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates linear probes as a method to study the geometric structures and arithmetic computations within large language models, addressing limitations of probe accuracy alone. It explores how internal representations in LLMs relate to their computational processes.

title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
summary: This paper introduces "One Tab", a new benchmark designed to evaluate generalist tabular models across generation, imputation, and prediction tasks. It aims to clarify shared capabilities and interaction of training objectives for models performing multiple tabular tasks.

title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
summary: This research introduces "Branch-and-Commit," a method for frozen reinforcement learning agents to spend test-time compute by sampling and evaluating multiple continuations from the current state. The approach helps select the optimal path when policies cannot be retrained or modified during deployment.

title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
summary: This research proposes using path signatures and a rough-path-theoretic perspective for trace-to-program induction, aiming to synthesize programs from execution traces. This method contributes to algorithmic interpretability and reverse engineering of complex systems.

title: FaST: Factored Synthesis of Transitions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents "FaST" (Factored Synthesis of Transitions), a new method for generating synthetic data for offline reinforcement learning that allows individual factors of a transition tuple to be redrawn in isolation. This approach aims to scale offline RL beyond fixed datasets by improving data augmentation.

title: Permutation-Based Pre-trained Model Merging via Reciprocal Orthogonality
summary: This research explores permutation-based pre-trained model merging via reciprocal orthogonality, building on the concept of linear mode connectivity (LMC) in wide neural networks. It investigates how models' parameters can be connected by low-loss linear paths.

title: Continuous-Time Set-Transformers for Asynchronous WiFi-IMU Indoor Localization
summary: This research proposes using continuous-time set-transformers for asynchronous WiFi-IMU indoor localization, addressing challenges posed by different sampling rates and misaligned sensor data. The method aims to improve indoor positioning accuracy by effectively integrating diverse sensor streams.

title: INTENT: Out-of-Sample, Out-of-Time, and Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequences
summary: This paper addresses challenges in evaluating foundation models on user event sequences, particularly for out-of-sample, out-of-time, and cold-start scenarios. It introduces "INTENT," a proposed method or framework for evaluating these models when deployed, where direct comparison across private data is difficult.

title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?
summary: This research investigates the role of temperature in inference-time sampling for large language models, questioning the efficacy of fixed-temperature schemes. It explores whether varying temperature across samples can enhance multi-sample inference by optimizing the balance between reliability and diversity.

title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
summary: This research proposes "Action-Sequence Alignment" for multi-turn on-policy distillation, a method to improve tool-use agents by selecting effective successful trajectories as references. The technique aims to reduce train-inference distribution mismatch by guiding student agents with validated hindsight.

title: Byzantine-Robust Muon: Resilient Momentum Orthogonalization for Distributed Learning
summary: This research introduces "Byzantine-Robust Muon," an enhanced optimizer for distributed learning that improves resilience against adversarial behavior and data heterogeneity. It builds upon the Muon optimizer, which uses Linear Minimization Oracle and momentum orthogonalization for large-scale learning.

title: RadRef: A Reference-Free Metric for Radiology Report Generation
summary: This paper introduces "RadRef," a novel reference-free metric for evaluating AI-generated radiology reports by scoring report claims against image-derived beliefs. This metric addresses the challenge of assessing report quality when a radiologist-authored reference is unavailable.

title: Making Strides in Symbolic Imitation Learning: Offline Demonstrations, Online Tuning
summary: This research introduces Symbolic Imitation Learning, a new approach for continuous control tasks that combines offline demonstrations with online tuning. It aims to bridge the gap between effective deep reinforcement learning and interpretable evolutionary methods.

title: Prediction-Powered LLM Ranking with Adaptively Collected Human Feedback
summary: This research proposes a prediction-powered method for ranking large language models using adaptively collected human feedback. The approach aims to improve the precision of LLM evaluations by efficiently prioritizing informative model comparisons to reduce the cost of human feedback.

title: Structured Kernel Surrogate Models for Multimodal Attribution
summary: This research investigates structured kernel surrogate models for multimodal attribution, a technique to measure how one data modality in a sample influences learning outcomes in other multimodal samples. The study addresses the problem of understanding modality redundancy in multimodal AI systems.

title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction
summary: This research proposes XAI-driven confidence estimation for out-of-distribution (OOD)-resilient runtime prediction in machine learning-based resource management models. The method aims to improve the reliability of predictions by distinguishing between reliable and catastrophic failures, unlike global error margins.

title: Audited Gradients, Anchored Policies: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Flow Control
summary: This research introduces "Audited Gradients, Anchored Policies," a model-based reinforcement learning approach for efficient flow control. The method aims to reduce the high cost of designing feedback controllers by mitigating failure modes introduced by differentiable surrogates.

title: Wrong the Same Way: Cross-Prompt Sharing Both Suppresses and Amplifies Reward Hacking in RLVR
summary: This research investigates reward hacking in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), exploring how cross-prompt sharing can both suppress and amplify this phenomenon. It examines the interaction between RL systems and imperfect verifiers in a controlled environment.

title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
summary: GigaEdge Spench is an open-source SDK providing capabilities for practical streaming speech enhancement on various devices, including neural denoising and acoustic echo cancellation. It allows developers to build applications leveraging these specific audio processing capabilities.

title: Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies
summary: This research explores "Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies" in reinforcement learning, introducing a method to balance bias and variance when learning a target policy from data generated by a different behavior policy. It examines linear interpolation between behavior and target policies.

title: An Analytical Model of Compute-limited Multistage Training Pipelines
summary: Modern foundation models are trained through multiple stages, yet how these stages interact and how compute should be allocated across them remain poorly understood. We introduce an analytically tractable high-dimensional model combining unsupervised pretraining with a linear autoencoder, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with noisy stepwise labels, and reinforcement learning (RL) with sparse episodic rewards. Using random matrix theory and an operator-projection closure, we derive approximate low-dimensional learning dynamics that closely match simulations. We show that finite pretraining data imposes a representation-dependent performance limit, with Bayes classification error scaling as the inverse square root of the pretraining sample ratio, and observe the same exponent in asymptotic SFT and RL errors. Better pretraining also reduces sensitivity to noisy supervision. SFT initialization shortens the initial RL plateau induced by sparse rewards, an effect we also observe in OLMo-2 1B on GSM8K. Longer SFT warm starts additionally improve asymptotic RL performance. Optimizing compute across all three stages reveals that the optimal allocation depends on supervision quality and total budget, with a non-monotonic dependence of the RL compute share on budget. Finally, a complementary compositional model shows how RL selectively strengthens task-relevant pretrained skills while largely preserving unused skills. Together, these results identify mechanisms linking representation quality, feedback structure, and compute allocation in multistage training.

title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Efficient Multipath Parameter Estimation in MIMO Systems
summary: High-resolution multipath estimation in wideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels requires repeated searches over angle of arrival, angle of departure, and propagation distance. This paper presents neural network-assisted CLEAN (NN-CLEAN), which replaces the multidimensional search at each extraction step with a multi-head classifier while retaining least-squares (LS) estimation of the complex path gain, parametric reconstruction, and residual cancellation. The same classifier is applied to successive residuals, allowing the extraction depth to vary without changing its output structure. With the number of iterations prescribed by the reference multipath-component (MPC) count, off-grid synthetic tests show that NN-CLEAN slightly exceeds grid-search CLEAN (GS-CLEAN) in path accuracy for one and two MPCs, although its accuracy declines more rapidly at larger path counts. For complete three-MPC extraction at a batch size of eight, NN-CLEAN achieves an approximately $27\times$ speedup and a $52$-fold reduction in peak GPU memory relative to GS-CLEAN. Applied without retraining to two-MPC line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) Sionna ray-tracing channels within a coded MIMO link, NN-CLEAN substantially reduces channel-reconstruction mean-squared error (MSE) and bit error rate (BER) relative to interpolated LS channel estimation. GS-CLEAN retains an accuracy advantage on these channels, indicating the estimation cost associated with the computational savings.

title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
summary: Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $\pi_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. Across 30 policy inputs from 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, the Jacobian exhibits strong contracting directions near the action endpoint, yet no sampled mode violates the Euler non-expansion condition. On five of those inputs, accuracy sweeps require 4--9 Euler steps at 5% terminal error and 87--112 at 1%. These five paired cases are therefore consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.

title: MicroLens: Read, Trace, and Rewire the Residual Stream with Two Lenses
summary: Lenses that decode hidden states into words are a popular way to look inside language models, but a heatmap of decoded words only shows what a vector reads as and cannot distinguish whether, or how much, the model uses the information. We present an interactive viewer that puts reading, tracing and editing on the same layers-by-tokens grid of the residual stream. In the viewer, every cell can be decoded with two lenses, the logit lens and the Jacobian lens (J-lens), traced back to the tokens it drew from, and edited, with the rest of the model rerun on the spot. We demonstrate three usage scenarios on Gemma-3-4B-it, backed by sweeps over a few hundred prompts, to show what this tool can discover. First, the two lenses give different directions to write with, each suiting a different edit: the logit lens's word direction sets what a token outputs, while the J-lens's direction changes what later tokens read. Second, in two-hop trivia questions (the capital of the state or country containing a given city), the state or country is readable at the city token from as early as layer 7, and swapping it there can redirect the answer 92-98% of the time; however, at the answer position, the state or country information is not used. Third, when a chat model answers questions with a step-by-step reasoning prompt, the correct answer is often already the top word in the residual stream before any reasoning is written: for 89-92% of retrieval questions and 39-63% of multi-hop and serial ones, far above their respective distractors (at most 5%). However, ordering puzzles are an exception, as the model works them out only once it writes its final reasoning steps. Furthermore, for answers that are visible in the residual stream, the J-lens reads them a layer or two earlier than the logit lens across the different types of question.

title: Robust Flow Matching under Target Corruption and Label Noise
summary: Flow Matching (FM) is a strong framework for generative modeling due to its stable training and efficient sampling. However, FM assumes clean target data and labels, an assumption often violated in practice. We formulate FM training as a time-dependent regression problem over conditional vector fields and analyze how the two corruption types affect the objective: i) target corruption adds a time-dependent residual term that grows with time, ii) label noise causes updates to the wrong class-conditional vector field. Based on this analysis, we propose to improve FM robustness by mapping corruption-specific residual scores to sample weights. For target corruption, we propose the Temporal Residual Score (TRS), which emphasizes residual magnitudes at intermediate-to-late FM times, where clean and corrupted samples are more separable. For label noise, we propose the Comparative Conditional Score (CCS), which compares the residual of the observed class-conditional vector field against alternative class-conditional vector fields for the same trajectory and velocity target. Experiments across controlled corruption settings and real-world noisy labels show that the proposed methods improve robustness over standard FM and robust-training baselines, supporting corruption-specific residual structure as a practical basis for robust FM.

title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
summary: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client level. This strategy decouples the $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ gradients, diminishes LoRA low-rank constraints and reduces both computational and uplink communication overheads by 50\%, allowing for the reallocation of resources toward higher adaptation ranks. Furthermore, we show that in this frozen-$\mathbf{A}$ regime, the adaptation rank $r$ directly governs the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the perturbed gradients. Specifically, we find that the SNR increases linearly with $r$, implying that clients' learning rates must be dynamically scaled with their adaptation ranks for higher utility. Building on these foundations, we introduce SPRA-LoRA (Stochastic Projection Rank-Aware LoRA), a federated rank-aware fine-tuning strategy that utilizes frozen, resampled $\mathbf{A}$ matrices and rank-dependent learning rates for clients. We also prove its convergence with heterogeneous client resources. Our experiments across benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPRA-LoRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with half the overhead on clients.

title: Advancing Mass-Conserving Deep Learning for Distributed Hydrologic Modeling: A Case Study in a Snow-Dominated Watershed
summary: Recent progress in physics-aware deep learning (DL) has embedded mass conservation within Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture for hydrologic modeling, improving physical consistency and enabling diagnostics of internal states. However, existing mass-conserving neural networks are primarily developed in lumped formulations. Consequently, previous studies provide only fragmented and often indirect evidence of when and why imposed physical constraints may lead to unrealistic hydrologic behavior. To address this limitation, we propose Physics-Enhanced Conservation-Augmented Net (PECAN), a mass-conserving convolutional LSTM-based framework for distributed hydrologic modeling and diagnosing structural limitations of physics-aware DL models. PECAN is implemented in two variants: (1) PECAN-MC with a strict precipitation-based conservation constraint and (2) PECAN-MCR with a relaxed conservation constraint allowing additional water inputs beyond precipitation. Both variants are trained solely on gauge streamflow and evaluated in a snow-dominated watershed in Colorado. We benchmark PECAN against lumped DL baselines and the distributed process-based Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model. Results show that PECAN achieves competitive outlet streamflow simulation accuracy while producing spatially explicit latent states for interpretation. Comparisons with reference soil moisture indicate that PECAN cell states resemble meaningful temporal soil moisture dynamics. However, analyses also reveal that PECAN misrepresents snow processes by prematurely removing winter snow water storage from the system rather than retaining it for spring release. PECAN demonstrates accurate streamflow simulation at gauges and shows diagnostic potential to expose structural limitations in hydrologic process representation, thereby informing future physics-aware neural network development for hydrology.

title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on IGRA Radiosonde Data
summary: Wind profiles in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) drive short-range forecasting and wind-energy siting, yet sparse radiosonde coverage forces practitioners to interpolate them from a handful of physical predictors. We benchmark modern tabular learners against analytical parameterizations on 158,097 IGRA soundings. CatBoost, TabM, and FT-Transformer reduce RMSE to 1.3-1.6 m/s, against approximately 3 m/s for power-law and Monin-Obukhov fits; once the predictor set is fixed the three architectures differ by less than 0.05 m/s, so accuracy is driven by predictors rather than architecture. A cohort analysis of within-bin profile dispersion places an empirical floor of approximately 1.77 m/s on any point-wise predictor that uses standard radiosonde features, consistent with prior eddy-viscosity inversions. A one-dimensional Fourier Neural Operator applied as a post-hoc corrector to frozen tabular predictions reduces near-surface RMSE on U.S. stations from 1.5 to 1.2 m/s, while leaving upper-layer error unchanged. Further gains should come from new predictors rather than larger models.

title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders
summary: Looped language models deepen computation without adding parameters, yet caching full-context key-value (KV) states across layers and rounds severely bounds serving batch size. We design a looped causal encoder-decoder (CED) that achieves recurrent depth with zero round-wise KV growth, addressing where and how to loop an asymmetric stack in which only sparse encoder layers generate global KV. We find that recurrence must be placed in the encoder to iteratively refine global KV representations rather than re-reading static decoder projections, which both drives language-modeling gains and preserves long-context scaling. Furthermore, training the encoder loop under stochastic recurrence depth induces a fixed-point equilibrium where every round losslessly shares the last round's KV cache. Compounding cross-layer and cross-round KV sharing, the resulting Looped CED matches an unlooped CED's minimal memory footprint and recovers 86-93% of a looped Transformer's gain with 1/6 of its global KV. To test serving at production scale, we loop the 552B-parameter DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash for 8 rounds on one 4xGB200 node: with per-layer and per-round KV the loop cannot fit a single 128K-token request, whereas Looped CED holds 36.8x less KV per token, fits 38 such requests (as many as the unlooped model), and serves 3.6x higher throughput on 8K-token prompts.

title: AdjointFlow: Accelerating Scientific Inverse Problems with Physics-Based Transport
summary: Inverse problems are ubiquitous across scientific applications ranging from seismic imaging to astrophysics to nondestructive testing, yet classical solvers often struggle with nonconvexity and repeated evaluations of expensive physical models. Diffusion models can amortize this computation offline, but largely data-driven conditional models underutilize known physics and suffer from ill-conditioned transport maps when the target distribution is concentrated. Plug-and-play (PnP) methods explicitly leverage the physical model to guide a learned prior, improving data consistency but reintroducing costly iterative computations. We instead propose AdjointFlow, a framework built on stochastic interpolants that injects the known physics into the generative transport itself. We design a data-dependent, adjoint-based initialization to reduce transport distance to the target, modify the transport velocity to remain regular as the endpoint distributions concentrate, and parameterize the network to build the initialization directly into the learned velocity. Together, these enable accurate reconstruction at substantially lower cost than generative models starting from Gaussian noise. Experiments on inverse scattering, seismic imaging, and black hole imaging show that AdjointFlow consistently produces more accurate reconstructions than conditional diffusion models while being up to five orders of magnitude faster at inference than PnP methods. Optional inference-time refinement that queries the physical model can further improve data consistency, matching or exceeding the accuracy of PnP methods without retraining.

title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning
summary: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute. Zero-cost signals such as mean token entropy and log-probability are local to tokens or to one completion, and self-consistency needs many extra completions. We show that Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for power sampling already estimates the normalizing constant of the power distribution, which gives the sequence-level R'enyi entropy (SRE) of the model's completion distribution at zero marginal cost, with a guarantee at every particle budget. A R'enyi chain rule extends this readout to a family of stepwise entropies of any order. We prove that orders above one are tied to the most likely token of each step, which explains why they track log-probability, while the order-1/2 member accumulates the log of per-step search effort. This member is the best zero-cost selective-prediction signal in 10 of 13 settings. On MATH500 its AUROC is 0.022 to 0.044 above log-probability with all four models and within length quartiles, and the same order is selected when each setting is held out. An 8-particle probe identifies the problems that benefit from more particles, and a two-pass policy matches 64-particle accuracy on MATH500 with 34.2% fewer particles over three seeds.

title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do In-Context Learning
summary: How should we understand memorization vs. generalization in in-context learning (ICL) tasks, and when does one happen vs. the other? To investigate, we study how rotation-invariant kernel machines learn the ICL linear regression task proposed by Raventos et al. (2023). By decomposing the task in the kernel eigenbasis, we obtain a spectral picture of learning in this ICL setting. This picture reveals that as sample size grows, kernel machines learn successively-higher-degree components of the memorizing solution, which depend upon successively-higher-degree statistics of the training task set. The generalizing solution is approximately a low-degree truncation of the memorizing solution, and so the model first generalizes, then degrades into memorization as training proceeds. The takeaways are threefold. First, if this case is indicative, learning a "generalizing" solution on an ICL task is really just underfitting the memorizing solution! Second, the fact that kernel machines can generalize on this task means that feature learning is inessential to ICL. Third, transformers empirically trained to do ICL are shown to memorize tasks through the higher-order statistics of the training tasks that the kernel-based theory predicts, suggesting it applies even to models capable of feature learning.

title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization
summary: Analog integrated circuit (IC) design is a multi-turn, simulator-grounded engineering task that demands iterative reasoning over coupled performance tradeoffs, yet proprietary process design kits (PDKs) make hosted large language model workflows difficult to deploy in practical design settings. We present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-scale, locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit optimization. SLIC pairs structured circuit representations with discretized relative-update actions, domain- and success-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering (RGRS), which turns per-step simulator feedback into signals for both policy learning and online rollout construction in this sparse, highly constrained domain. We further release an open, goal-conditioned benchmark of 41 amplifier topologies with standardized protocols for in-distribution validation, held-out topology evaluation, and cross-technology-node transfer. Trained solely with open source 65 nm CMOS predictive technology models (PTM), SLIC-Random achieves 87.1% in-distribution four-specification Pass@1 within eight turns, surpassing the 763B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Think by 48.5 percentage points. Beyond the training distribution, SLIC-Softmax reaches 72.6% Pass@1 on held-out topologies, and the trained policies consistently transfer across five unseen technology nodes without additional fine-tuning. This transfer extends to a commercial TSMC 65 nm CMOS PDK, where SLIC-Random achieves 49.9% held-out-topology Pass@1, demonstrating practical deployment through local inference without transmitting proprietary data to external LLM services. Performance further scales with test-time simulator interactions, reaching up to 83.2% held-out-topology Pass@1 at a 32-turn budget.

title: Deep Personalization: Continuous Context Observation for Local Proactive Agents
summary: As AI agents become increasingly capable, users must still recognize when and how to ask for help, leaving many opportunities for useful support unrealized. Proactive agents hold the promise to close this gap, but effective proactivity requires understanding users' real-time activities and personalizing intervention timing so that assistance is offered when it is likely to be helpful rather than disruptive. We introduce deep personalization, a closed-loop process that connects continuous context observation with continual agent adaptation: an agent observes user activity, selectively retains long-term context, and adapts intervention decisions from implicit feedback. We initiate deep personalization in Coco, a proactive desktop agent, by having a separate Observer Agent that monitors desktop activity, maintains compact long-term user modeling context, and learns when assistance is desirable from implicit signals such as engagement, dismissal, explicit requests, and repeated work patterns. We further develop efficient on-device strategies to enable the Observer Agent to run on local AI compute platforms without streaming raw activity data off-device. For evaluation at scale without collecting sensitive real-user activity, we introduce a data-synthesis pipeline that transforms existing computer-use trajectories into OSWorld-Persona, a benchmark with persona-conditioned intervention labels. On OSWorld-Persona, deep personalization improves macro F1 across three model backbones from 0.12-0.19 under direct prompting to 0.35-0.48 after adaptation, a 2.4-3.0x relative gain. In a week-long user study, we observe that Coco improves its macro-averaged F1 score from 0.199 to 0.515. These results suggest that on-device deep personalization can make proactive agents more timely and increasingly aligned with each user's everyday work.

title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling
summary: Integrating human feedback into language models has gained increasing attention as a means to align model outputs with human preferences, with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) serving as a prominent framework for preference-based alignment. Recent studies have incorporated eye-tracking (ET) data as an additional supervisory signal for reward model training, grounding reward learning in human reading behavior. Building on this approach, we extend prior fixation-centric models by leveraging established findings from cognitive psychology on human letter recognition. Specifically, we model visual attention as a spatially graded distribution centered on the current gaze location and incorporate this representation into reward model training. Our results show that the reward model trained with the proposed gaze distribution achieves higher preference prediction accuracy than a baseline model. Moreover, some results from our experiments are qualitatively consistent with established findings on human attention during reading, suggesting that they potentially capture cognitively meaningful aspects of human attention allocation.

title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
summary: KL-regularized reinforcement learning, the objective behind maximum-entropy RL and RL from human feedback, is variational inference in the graphical model of "control as inference": the regularized optimal policy is a posterior over trajectories, and the suboptimality of a policy is $\beta$ times a KL divergence between path measures. However, it is not known how many samples it takes to learn this posterior, even with a generative model. Earlier $1/\epsilon$ guarantees scale with $H^5$ in the effective horizon $H$, and no lower bound for MDPs depends on the temperature $\beta$. In this work, we show that for a discounted MDP with $K$ state-action pairs, the plug-in estimator finds a policy that is $\epsilon$-optimal from every initial state with $\widetilde{O}(KH^3/(\epsilon\max\{\epsilon,\beta\}) + KH)$ samples, and that no algorithm, even one that chooses where to sample, can do with fewer when $\epsilon \lesssim \min\{H, H^2/\beta\}$. For $\epsilon < \beta$ this is a $1/\epsilon$ rate with the same horizon dependence as unregularized RL. We also find the exact asymptotic constant of the plug-in estimator, a Fisher-weighted variance of the estimated soft Q-function. The estimator is locally asymptotically minimax among methods that sample every pair equally often, and we give the allocation of samples that is optimal among adaptive designs. Simulations on small MDPs match the rates and the constants.

title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
summary: Compositional generalization is an important form of out-of-distribution generalization, defined as the ability to train on some combinations of modules (e.g., functions such as sort, filter) and then generalize to unseen combinations. Despite substantial empirical work evaluating compositional generalization in transformers, findings have been inconsistent because evaluations were often conducted on a limited set of train-test splits, defined in an ad hoc manner. Through a systematic evaluation, we identify two key aspects of the train-test distribution that strongly affect performance: composition equivalence and module coverage. We show that the apparent performance of direct models (trained only on final outputs) results primarily from exploiting composition equivalences, meaning different sequences of modules that reduce to identical end-to-end functions. When benchmarks eliminate these equivalences, performance drops significantly, showing their inability to generalize to compositions of known modules that produce novel end-to-end functions. We further demonstrate that performance degrades monotonically as module coverage shifts increase (when modules appear in different contexts between train and test), affecting both direct and step-by-step models (trained on intermediate and final outputs). These findings have concrete implications for benchmark design: benchmarks that include compositional equivalences can lead to significant overestimation of the generalization abilities of direct models, and benchmarks that include both module coverage violations and compositional equivalences can exacerbate shortcut learning. As a case study, we demonstrate the role of compositional equivalence on the generalization performance of the pre-trained model Llama3-8B on the code-output prediction task in the coding benchmark LiveCodeBench.

title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
summary: Nonlinear state space models are typically evaluated sequentially, limiting their ability to exploit modern parallel hardware. Recent work has shown that state space models can be evaluated in parallel by reformulating evaluation as a root-finding problem, which can be solved with a parallel form of Newton's method. However, exact Newton methods require expensive multiplication of dense Jacobian matrices, and quasi-Newton methods based on diagonal approximations, while more scalable, are often slow to converge because they neglect interactions across state dimensions. We introduce a novel quasi-Newton approach based on Broyden's method, which captures coupling terms with diagonal-plus-low-rank approximations to blocks of the Jacobian. We construct the approximations from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation while retaining the favorable scaling of diagonal approximations and remaining compatible with parallel scan through rank compression. We prove finite-step recovery of the exact trajectory under the compressed scan, and show that convergence is tracked by the compression error and by the block approximation error along the current trajectory error, rather than in spectral norm. Empirically, we show that our method is advantageous when interactions are approximately low rank or when Jacobian evaluation is expensive: on low-rank RNNs, parallel MCMC algorithms, and denoising diffusion models, it converges in fewer iterations than other quasi-Newton methods and is the fastest parallel method when Jacobian evaluation is expensive or state dimensions are large.

title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to improve an agent using its own task experience. Its practical value depends on whether performance gains justify the full cost of self-improvement and task execution. We evaluate this trade-off on continual task streams, scoring each task before its feedback is used for subsequent updates. We define the \emph{RSI Tax} as the token cost of the self-improvement process and include it alongside task-execution costs in end-to-end evaluation. Across six methods and two language models, a bounded-note baseline matches or exceeds the observed accuracy of Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI, with mean total-token savings of 65.6-71.0\%. We decompose the RSI Tax into verification, exploration, and writing costs, and track subsequent use of the associated state or artifact. For these three RSI methods, verification accounts for 74.8--93.6% of the aggregate RSI Tax. A substantial share of the RSI Tax is also associated with states or artifacts that are not used later in the evaluated streams. These results expose a practical limitation of costly RSI procedures: improvements in the deployed agent need not justify the expense of the improvement process. They motivate RSI objectives that jointly optimize the RSI Tax and expected task-execution cost while ensuring continued growth in agent capabilities across the task stream.

title: Adaptive catalyst discovery emerges from composable scientific intelligence
summary: Catalysis underpins chemical manufacturing, yet knowledge for catalyst design remains dispersed across experimental observations, computational data and catalysis subdisciplines. To overcome this challenge, we present Composable Catalytic Intelligence (CatAI), a physics-grounded modular AI framework that learns 1.8 million structure-property relations and organizes them into 30 physicochemical encoders. This reusable intermediate layer enables task-specific models to guide catalyst discovery for targeted reactions and objectives. Across benchmark tasks, CatAI achieves a 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models. In experimental validation, CatAI identified a new confined-passable pocket catalyst applicable in industrial homogeneous polymer synthesis with 9 times the activity of the commercial benchmark. In parallel, it guided autonomous closed-loop optimization of a highly active Cu-based geminal-atom photocatalyst for C-O coupling reactions surpassing the traditional Ni-based systems. This approach connects property-level data to catalytic objectives, supporting physicochemical knowledge reuse across mechanistically distinct systems through computational screening and iterative model-experiment feedback.

title: Sanity Checks for Attention Surgery: Null Models and Matched Interventions for Representation-Motivated Design
summary: This research paper proposes methods to evaluate architectural modifications in transformers by checking if observed statistics exceed noise floors and survive geometric transformations.

title: Closing the BF16-FP16 Convergence Speed Gap in RL Post-Training with Stochastic Rounding
summary: This paper investigates how stochastic rounding can close the convergence speed gap between BF16 and FP16 mixed-precision training in reinforcement learning.

title: From Relevant Posts to Attributable Spans: Explicit Symptom Evidence for Depression Questionnaire Inference
summary: This research explores using longitudinal social media histories to infer standardized depression questionnaire responses by identifying relevant and attributable symptom evidence.

title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
summary: This paper proposes a step-aware decoding method to mitigate hallucinations in multimodal diffusion language models by analyzing mask uncertainty during iterative denoising.

title: TimeOmni-o1: Bidirectionally Coupling Time Series Foundation Models and LLMs for Multimodal Reasoning and Forecasting
summary: This research introduces TimeOmni-o1, a method for bidirectionally coupling time series foundation models and LLMs to perform multimodal reasoning and forecasting on time series data accompanied by text.

title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
summary: This paper introduces SELD, a method for detecting silent evidence loss in context compression for language models, which occurs when key evidence is removed without affecting the immediate answer.

title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
summary: This research investigates how user edit data from clinicians reviewing LLM outputs in clinical documentation workflows can be leveraged as actionable feedback for improving model capabilities.

title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
summary: This work introduces Brasilidade, a new benchmark and assessment methodology with standardized tasks across four domains, designed to measure Brazilian identity in large language models.

title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
summary: This paper proposes sparse target optimization as a new approach for knowledge editing in large language models, aiming to efficiently update embedded knowledge by computing an ideal target hidden state.

title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter
summary: This paper introduces khammoon, a new Thai morpheme segmenter developed from linguistic guidelines, addressing the challenges of word segmentation in Thai NLP due to the absence of spaces.

title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
summary: This paper measures the tokenization disparity for nine public tokenizers, including GPT-4, showing that Indian languages require significantly more tokens than English for the same content, leading to higher costs.

title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
summary: This paper introduces Havon v3, a new byte-level BPE tokenizer for 204 languages that uses fewer tokens than GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, particularly benefiting Indian languages.

title: Catch It Where It Happens: Real Time Error Correction During LLM Reasoning
summary: This paper presents a method for real-time error correction during large language model reasoning to prevent the propagation of mistakes, especially in mathematical, scientific, and engineering tasks.

title: HiCAP: Hierarchical Cultural Adaptation via Personality for Dialogue Generation
summary: This paper introduces HiCAP, a method for hierarchical cultural adaptation in dialogue generation systems that leverages personality to create responses conforming to cultural linguistic norms and social expectations.

title: What drives the emergence of symbolic mechanisms in large language models?
summary: This research investigates the factors driving the emergence of symbolic mechanisms that support abstract reasoning in large language models by training neural networks on abstract sequence tasks.

title: Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts
summary: This paper measures the definition sensitivity of large language models when annotating social science concepts, analyzing how prompt definitions influence the accuracy of the assigned labels.

title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis
summary: This paper analyzes online forum discussions to understand instructors' perspectives on the rationales students provide for engaging in AI-mediated cheating in academic settings.

title: Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis
summary: This exploratory analysis uses forum data to map instructors' attitudes towards cheating with AI and the challenges it presents to academic integrity in teaching and learning environments.

title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces BioMem, an agentic memory system designed to enhance the ability of biomedical large language model agents to preserve and utilize information across tasks and interactions.

title: Inherited Weights: Measuring the Tokenization Premium and the Sovereignty Cost of Language Models for the Global South
summary: This paper examines how fine-tuning leaves language models with inherited properties like vocabulary and cultural alignment from their base models, discussing the "tokenization premium" and "sovereignty cost" for the Global South.

title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
summary: This paper introduces Mobile AI Factory, a framework for building and fine-tuning specialized small language models (SLMs) for mobile devices, optimizing for privacy and offline functionality.

title: Framing-Induced Vulnerability in Large Language Models: Evidence from Chinese News Headlines
summary: This research investigates how large language models (LLMs) judge Chinese news headlines, revealing vulnerabilities where model judgment is influenced more by framing than by reported facts.

title: How Post-Training Influences Verbalized Algorithmic Computation in Language Models
summary: This study examines how post-training methods like SFT, DPO, and RLVR influence the internal information usage and verbalized chain of thought in language models during reasoning tasks.

title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
summary: This research explores the effectiveness of dense process rewards compared to token-based credit in Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for training language models to reason.

title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
summary: This introduces Med Evidence Bench (MEB), a new evidence-traceable benchmark with 1,536 physician-constructed items designed to evaluate clinical reasoning in large language models.

title: A Concept-Based Interpretable Framework for Clinical Text-based Prediction via Token-Concept Attention without Concept Supervision
summary: This paper presents a novel concept-based interpretable framework for clinical text prediction that uses token-concept attention without requiring concept supervision, addressing a key challenge in model explainability.

title: IFRS Compliance Verification: An Open Multi-LLM Benchmark and Content-Conditioned Ensemble Classifier
summary: This introduces an open multi-LLM benchmark and a content-conditioned ensemble classifier designed to verify corporate financial disclosures against International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

title: Compute the Interactions, Not the Attributes: What a Fact Layer Must Supply in the Chinese Sexagenary System
summary: This research measures which facts a deterministic fact layer should supply to language models in rule-governed domains, using the Chinese sexagenary system as a case study.

title: One Byte, One Token: Byteifying a 27B Hybrid-Attention LLM with Self-Generated Data
summary: This research explores converting an already-trained 27B subword hybrid-attention language model directly into a pure byte-level model using self-generated data.

title: Post-OCR Correction of Mixed-Script Uzbek Text: Byte-Level ByT5 with an Empirical Homoglyph Noise Matrix
summary: This paper proposes a post-OCR correction method for mixed-script Uzbek text using Byte-Level ByT5 and an empirical homoglyph noise matrix to address specific error types.

title: Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control
summary: This presents Synapse-Control, an agent runtime designed to make large language model agent execution experience actionable and improve reliability on complex tool-based tasks with lightweight control.

title: An Interpretable Stylometric Framework for Early Chinese Buddhist Translator Styles: A Case Study on the Attribution of Disputed Works of An Shigao
summary: This paper develops an interpretable stylometric framework using philologist-defined features to attribute disputed early Chinese Buddhist translations, focusing on the works of An Shigao.

title: OpticalRAG: Pixel-Space Compression for Token-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This introduces OpticalRAG, a novel approach that uses pixel-space compression for token-efficient retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to overcome the limitations of token budgets in large language models.

title: You Are What You Read: Indian Political News Media Bias Dataset for Hindi Language
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive, multi-annotator, explainable dataset for understanding and detecting political news media bias in the Hindi language within the Indian context.

title: Do Language Models Feel the Sentiment? Investigating Emotion Vectors
summary: This study investigates emotion vectors within language models, exploring their presence in internal representations and their role in influencing sentiment classification behavior in models like Qwen2.

title: Word-Level Alignment of OCR and Ground Truth under Zoning and Reading-Order Errors
summary: This research revisits the problem of word-level alignment between OCR output and ground truth, proposing a protocol to handle zoning and reading-order errors effectively in OCR post-processing.

title: LLM Validation Makes Minimal-Pair Benchmarks Easier for Language Models
summary: This research explores using large language models (LLMs) to validate minimal-pair benchmarks, testing this method on BLiMP and QFrBLiMP datasets to make benchmark creation more efficient.

title: Antalia-2 Mini: A 7.6-million-parameter Turkish text-to-speech model trained entirely on synthetic speech
summary: Antalia-2 Mini is introduced as a 7.6-million-parameter Turkish text-to-speech model, trained entirely on synthetic speech, capable of producing 48 kHz audio efficiently.

title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
summary: PolyRoute is released as a new benchmark for typed-decision routing across twelve languages and code-mixed inputs, providing baselines and a leaderboard for evaluation.

title: Alania-2: Turkish text-to-speech with instant and fine-tuned voice cloning
summary: Alania-2 is presented as a 488M-parameter Turkish text-to-speech (TTS) system featuring two built-in voices, voice design from text descriptions, and instant and fine-tuned voice cloning capabilities.

title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
summary: This paper proposes an on-policy mid-training distillation method for continual pre-training of large language models, adapting them to specialized domains more effectively.

title: Beyond Fluent Responses: Finding User Dissatisfaction in Human-AI Interactions
summary: This research explores user-centered criteria for evaluating large language model responses, focusing on identifying user dissatisfaction in human-AI interactions beyond basic fluency.

title: AVCC: Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction with a Human Benchmark
summary: This work introduces the AVCC (Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus), a new public dataset with a human benchmark for predicting turn-taking in multiparty conversations, relevant for conversational agents and social robots.

title: On the information rate of phones, syllables and words
summary: This study investigates which linguistic units (phones, syllables, words) minimize the bitrate for encoding speech content, exploring implications for speech systems and human language processing theories.

title: One Sequence Is Enough: Fingerprinting Language Models from Fixed-Length Integer Sequences
summary: This research proposes a method for 'fingerprinting' language models based on their fixed-length integer sequence outputs, allowing for identity verification when models are accessed via APIs.

title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
summary: This research explores 'agent skills' for LLM agents, detailing how program-aided, patchable skill evolution allows agents to solve complex tasks by distilling reusable knowledge from execution.

title: MISO-BR: An Open Corpus for Misogyny Detection in Brazilian Portuguese
summary: This paper introduces MISO-BR, an open, documented, and versioned corpus of 896 social media texts in Brazilian Portuguese annotated for binary misogyny detection.

title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
summary: This project developed and evaluated HandsOnAid, an offline first-aid assistant based on a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned for emergency response scenarios without phone signal.

title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
summary: This paper critically examines the concept of 'bias' in machine learning systems and proposes a 'positionality' framework for understanding Large Language Models.

title: Sckwoky at SHROOM-Visions: Character-Level Hallucination-Span Detection in Image-Conditioned VLMs via Dual-Prompted LoRA Decoders
summary: This describes a system for character-level hallucination span detection in image-conditioned vision-language models, built on a frozen Gemma-4-12B-it backbone for a shared task.

title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks
summary: This research investigates the 'representational atoms' within neural networks to understand how learned knowledge is organized and its relationship with human conceptual structure.

title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
summary: This study analyzes the stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation within Transformer-based language models as they learn to handle syntactic structures.

title: StaRSE: Compact Russian Sentence Embeddings with a Sign-Coded Static Encoder
summary: This paper introduces StaRSE, a compact Russian static sentence encoder designed to remove Transformer inference at deployment time for efficient sentence embedding on CPUs.

title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
summary: This paper introduces DyShip, a framework that leverages acoustic features to classify speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations.

title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
summary: This paper presents an AI assistant based on the TRACE framework designed to automate anti-corruption expertise by screening draft legislation for corruption risks.

title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
summary: This research discusses 'Point-in-Time Encoders' for earnings calls, detailing how text encoders should be trained for accurate financial search, RAG, and forecasting in backtesting scenarios.

title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research proposes an 'overlapping block denoising' technique to enhance the efficiency of Diffusion Language Models for faster token generation in latency-critical tasks.

title: Uncovering the Blind Spots of OKS-mAP: A Unified Protocol for Occlusion, Joint-Angle, and Temporal Evaluation of 2D Pose Estimators
summary: This paper proposes a unified protocol to supplement OKS-mAP, addressing its blind spots in evaluating 2D pose estimators for occlusion, joint-angle error, and temporal stability.

title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
summary: This paper introduces URL-Sim, a unified and regulated LiDAR simulation method for high-fidelity reconstruction of dynamic driving scenes, essential for validating autonomous driving systems.

title: Attribute-Evidence Learning with Multimodal Prompt for Generalized Category Discovery
summary: This paper proposes an attribute-evidence learning method with multimodal prompts to discover novel categories from unlabeled data, leveraging limited labeled samples from old classes.

title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
summary: This paper introduces a method to improve open-vocabulary object detection by preserving novel category capacity, addressing the bias of learned embeddings towards base categories.

title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
summary: This research explores trajectory-regularized distribution distillation for one-step generation, comparing trajectory alignment and distribution matching paradigms for flow matching models.

title: Evidence-Grounded Iterative Reasoning for the Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases
summary: This paper proposes using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for evidence-grounded iterative reasoning to improve the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases.

title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
summary: This paper introduces TIB, a sample-wise tempered information bottleneck method for multimodal attribution, to interpret models beyond the assumption of semantic alignment in paired modalities.

title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
summary: This paper presents PhysMoE, a method for fast spatial grounding in modality-decoupled VLMs using single-token coordinate representation to address bottlenecks in coordinate prediction for robotic tasks.

title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
summary: This paper introduces G-STAR, a group-scaled token capacity method for deeply compressed autoregressive generation, addressing the trade-off between representation quality and generation speed in discrete models.

title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
summary: GTAGym is introduced as a new environment using real AAA game tasks for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control in reinforcement learning, addressing challenges in automated task outcome verification.

title: MICRO: A Surgery-Phase Retinal Image Rigid Registration Benchmark and One-Step Frequency-Structure Similarity Registration Learning
summary: MICRO is presented as a new benchmark for multimodal retinal image rigid registration (MRIRG) in ophthalmic surgery, along with a one-step frequency-structure similarity registration learning method.

title: SpatialSR: Spatial Resolution-Centric Pipeline for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution
summary: This paper introduces SpatialSR, a spatial resolution-centric pipeline for arbitrary-scale remote sensing super-resolution that focuses on the absolute spatial resolution rather than just the relative scale factor.

title: Just Image Transformers with Late-Stage Pixel Refinement
summary: This research demonstrates the feasibility of training image generators using latent-free diffusion transformers with late-stage pixel refinement, avoiding VAE compression artifacts and simplifying the pipeline.

title: VIGOR: Benchmarking Visual Rationale Correctness in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: VIGOR is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the visual rationale correctness in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), assessing if their outputs are supported by appropriate visual evidence.

title: Continuous Angular Control in Text-to-Image Generation via Geometric Token Encoding
summary: This paper introduces a method for continuous angular control in text-to-image generation using geometric token encoding, enabling models to accurately render specific orientations, such as clock hands.

title: GroundCascade: Selective Second Opinions for GUI Grounding
summary: GroundCascade is introduced as a training-free controller that uses selective second opinions for GUI grounding, mapping screenshots and natural-language instructions to specific screen locations.

title: Multimodal Judges Flag, Humans Decide: A Review-and-Edit Framework for AI-Generated Product Video Ads
summary: This paper describes a review-and-edit framework for AI-generated product video ads, utilizing "multimodal judges" to flag content and humans to make final decisions and refine the output.

title: X Marks the Spot: Diffusion for Image Geolocalization with Location Representations
summary: This paper presents a diffusion-based method called X Marks the Spot for image geolocalization that uses location representations to accurately predict the origin of a photo.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Geographic Atrophy Segmentation in En Face OCT Images
summary: This study provides a comparative evaluation of deep learning models for segmenting Geographic Atrophy (GA) in en-face OCT images, a crucial step for diagnosing age-related macular degeneration.

title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
summary: This paper introduces a multimodal road closure mapping system that uses cross-modal graph attention to integrate visual evidence, spatial context, and road network topology for accurate identification.

title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
summary: This paper evaluates nonverbal social reasoning in early childhood, highlighting a gap in existing multimodal video understanding benchmarks which often neglect critical nonverbal cues like gaze and gesture.

title: Rethinking Evaluation for Video Capsule Endoscopy: Validation Protocol, Source-Video Diversity, and Cross-Dataset Shift
summary: This paper rethinks evaluation methods for automated video capsule endoscopy (VCE) classification, addressing challenges like class imbalance and dataset shift. It proposes a new validation protocol for deep learning models in this domain.

title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
summary: This research introduces adaptive residual quantization for memory-efficient temporal action segmentation, addressing the bottleneck of storing large pre-extracted frame features. The method aims to prevent catastrophic forgetting in long-form video tasks.

title: Domain adaptation of a video Foundation model for Heart Failure Diagnosis from Echocardiography
summary: This research explores the domain adaptation of a video foundation model for heart failure diagnosis using echocardiography. It investigates fine-tuning a pretrained foundation model for spatio-temporal medical imaging applications.

title: DUO: Dual Readouts of Diffusion Models for OOD Detection
summary: This paper introduces DUO, a method leveraging dual readouts of diffusion models to improve out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. This allows for safer deployment of generative diffusion models by identifying inputs outside their training distribution.

title: Domain-Adversarial Adaptation from MURA to In-House Radiographs for Improved Adult Elbow Fracture Classification
summary: This research investigates domain-adversarial adaptation to improve adult elbow fracture classification from radiographs, addressing domain shift between large public datasets and smaller institution-specific datasets. It uses a domain-adversarial neural network (DANN) for feature alignment.

title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
summary: This paper introduces ABRR, a new method transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) by localizing video segments corresponding to natural language queries. It uses Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking for improved video understanding applications.

title: How Hyperbolic Are Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models?
summary: This research investigates the practical "hyperbolicity" of hyperbolic vision-language models (VLMs). It examines their interpretable embedding spaces and the ordering of representations by generality in these models.

title: Prompt2Echo (P2Echo): Text-Prompted Multi-View Echocardiography Segmentation with One Model
summary: This paper presents P2Echo, a unified text-prompted framework for multi-view echocardiography segmentation. This method aims to improve automated cardiac assessment by handling anatomical and appearance variability with a single model.

title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
summary: This paper introduces Camera3R, a method for feed-forward 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous camera models using unconstrained multi-view images. It contributes to 3D computer vision research.

title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video
