title: DeltaVisionX: A Low-Cost Vision-Guided Automation System Using YOLOv11 and PLC-Based Actuation
summary: This paper presents DeltaVisionX, a low-cost industrial automation system that integrates real-time computer vision with PLC-based actuation for object classification and sorting. The system uses the YOLOv11 (You Only Look Once) deep learning model to detect objects on an operating conveyor belt and communicates detection results to a Delta DVP-SE PLC, which actuates pneumatic pistons for sorting. A custom dataset was created, labeled, and augmented to train the YOLOv11 model, achieving a mean average precision of 0.97 with real-time inference of 100 ms per frame. Encoder-based tracking ensures reliable synchronization between detection and actuation, supporting a throughput of 80 objects per minute. Results show that affordable, locally developed automation can reduce labor dependency and improve manufacturing efficiency. The novelty of the proposed system lies in its encodersynchronized vision-PLC integration rather than in the detection model itself. Future work includes integrating a highspeed Delta robot with EtherCAT-based servo control for advanced pick-and-place operations.

title: Analyzing Learning-Dynamics Across Loss and Prediction Choices for Diffusion Models
summary: Denoising generative models predict clean data ($x$), noise ($\epsilon$), or velocity ($v$), while training losses can be measured in any of these spaces. Although the resulting nine combinations are algebraically related, they can yield substantially different denoising accuracy and sample quality. We disentangle the effects of prediction and loss spaces. For a fixed prediction target, we show that changing the loss space is exactly equivalent to timestep reweighting and provide a heuristic analysis of how this reweighting affects generation quality. We then show that a rank-$m$ linear bottleneck compressing a $D$-dimensional noisy input imposes an irreducible squared-error floor of $D-m$ on noise and velocity prediction, whereas clean-data prediction can exploit low-dimensional data structure. Combining this bound with prediction-dependent error conversion yields distinct necessary conditions on bottleneck capacity. Experiments with U-Net and JiT across CIFAR-10, Imagenette, and ImageNet-256 support these theoretical predictions. Under compression, prediction choice strongly affects both denoising accuracy and sample quality, with noise-prediction errors closely matching the theoretical lower bound. Our results provide a quantitative understanding of how architectural bottlenecks interact with prediction and loss choices in denoising generative models.

title: RiverScan: Learning to Accumulate on River Networks
summary: Accurate runoff prediction across large river basins requires models to capture heterogeneous local hydrological responses and their accumulation downstream. River-network connectivity provides a natural structure for this task, but using it effectively requires learning how to combine contributions from subcatchments of different sizes. We frame this challenge as learning to accumulate and introduce RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence. RiverScan recursively combines local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states in topological order. Contributing-area fractions account for subcatchment size, while learned retention controls how upstream information persists downstream. Experiments on 608 stations in the Danube basin show that RiverScan outperforms the evaluated temporal and graph baselines in overall predictive performance. Structural controls and ablations demonstrate that composing heterogeneous subcatchment representations in a manner aligned with hydrological accumulation substantially improves runoff prediction, with the benefits of correct topology growing along the river-network hierarchy. These findings establish physically structured accumulation as an effective inductive bias for hydrological modeling and motivate finer-grained, fully distributed AI-based hydrological models.

title: Sample-Efficient Control of Magnetoconvective Flows via Differentiable Simulation
summary: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid flows are central to demanding engineering applications, most prominently fusion blanket cooling, where flow control is a promising tool to optimize key properties such as heat transfer. While active flow control (AFC) has recently advanced through machine learning, its application to MHD flows remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present $\phi$-PICT, a novel differentiable GPU-accelerated MHD solver targeted at AFC. We validate $\phi$-PICT against MHD benchmarks and demonstrate its high computational efficiency. Integrated into FluidGym, $\phi$-PICT enables sample-efficient gradient-based algorithms to improve heat transfer by $>25$% and allows optimizers to achieve $10^3\times$ higher accuracy in inverse design than black-box methods. $\phi$-PICT is publicly available at https://github.com/upb-sciml/phiPICT.

title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
summary: On-device reinforcement learning runs a periodic actor and a learner on one embedded GPU shared with other workloads. Because the learner produces the actor's weights, existing designs stall the actor or let its policy drift. We present RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$, an on-device runtime that makes this coupling a tunable parameter: a refresh bound limits actor releases between refreshes, and a GPU permit with slack-aware admission prioritises the actor and fills spare time with training atop any base scheduler. Under the real refresh cost on two Jetson boards, RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$ keeps a 16.8 M-parameter policy's deadline misses below 1%, against 85 to 100% without it.

title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
summary: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

title: Learning nonlinear interactions and cross-feature couplings with product-unit residual networks
summary: Understanding nonlinear feature interactions is crucial in science and engineering, yet standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) often capture such interactions only implicitly, leading to entangled representations that can impair robustness and interpretability. We investigate complex-valued product-unit residual networks (CV-PURe) that integrate multiplicative product units with residual connections to explicitly model cross-feature couplings while stabilizing optimization. We conduct a systematic evaluation on an interaction-driven synthetic benchmark and real-world datasets and evaluate prediction together with input-level interaction recovery under a reproducible protocol. Across five data splits and five training seeds, CV-PURe achieves the lowest mean RMSE on four of six scientific benchmarks, reducing Friedman error by 53.9% relative to MLP. Its Friedman interaction maps assign 60.7% of total strength to the known interacting pair, compared with 31.0% for MLP. On a synthetic task containing third- and fourth-order products and 20 distractors, CV-PURe reduces RMSE from 0.1376 to 0.0797 relative to a complex-valued MLP and recovers all nine true pairwise projections in every training/sampling repetition. Bike Sharing experiments connect improved prediction to the contribution of temporal, calendar, and seasonal context through paired ablations of both PURe variants. Parkinsons Telemonitoring extends the context analysis to repeated measurements. Noise and learning-curve evaluations demonstrate sustained predictive gains under perturbed inputs and limited supervision, while inference measurements quantify computational cost. This article extends our ICCS 2026 paper, Modeling Nonlinear Feature Interactions with Product-Unit Residual Networks (doi:10.1007/978-3-032-29921-5_6).

title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
summary: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. Here, we propose an alternative view, building on the principle that the correlations of a sequence reflect the structure of the process that generated it. We define the autocorrelation function of a layer as the average dot product between its activations at two context positions separated by a lag. Latent variables encoded persistently along the context create slowly decaying tails in the autocorrelation, and we find these tails to grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. In synthetic data with controlled hierarchical latent structure, this growth stems from the encoding of abstract latent variables, which govern long stretches of the input. Indeed, the persistence of latent codes predicts the qualitative structure of autocorrelations and accounts for most of the empirical measures. In real text, we take sparse-autoencoder features as proxies for latent variables, and find that their persistence correlates strongly with the magnitude of autocorrelations across datasets and LLMs. In particular, the persistence time increases with depth, as do autocorrelations, implying that deeper latent features persist for longer context spans. We complement this analysis by explicitly ablating the persistent sparse-autoencoder features and observing a consequent decrease in the autocorrelations.

title: Efficient Poincar\'e Convolutions through Patch-Statistics Factorization
summary: Published implementations of the Poincar\'e convolution in Hyperbolic Neural Networks++ (HNN++) map every overlapping image patch to the Poincar\'e ball before evaluating its score. We show that the clipped score depends on each patch only through two statistics, its squared norm and its inner products with the filters, which a native convolution and a single-channel box filter compute directly. The factorized layer therefore evaluates the specified score exactly, without constructing ball-valued patches, and its single-precision outputs and gradients agree with double-precision evaluations at least as closely as those of the explicit reference. On an RTX A6000 under two versions of JAX, complete training updates of a Poincar\'e U-Net and a Poincar\'e ResNet-20 are 1.5 to 1.8 times faster than the faster of two explicit implementations that map patches to the ball (1.2 to 1.4 times against an explicit implementation that skips this mapping); on a V100, the gain over the gather-based one persists as the ResNet-20 is widened eightfold. In 15 paired training runs per task, updates are 2.0 and 1.8 times faster than a reference that follows the published execution order, with no consistent change in final segmentation or classification quality, and peak memory falls by 38 to 55% in a U-Net scaling study. Replacing the convolutions of the official PyTorch Hyperbolic U-Net makes its training step 1.4 times faster with half the memory. Evaluating an existing layer from its patch statistics thus makes Poincar\'e convolutional networks cheaper to train in the tested models and software stacks.

title: When Copying Is Hard to Beat: A Negative Result in Clinical Assessment Forecasting
summary: We report a negative result in next-day clinical assessment forecasting: the evaluated models show no consistent advantage over strong persistence-based baselines. Clinicians can view the previous day's questionnaire answers, a plausible source of documentation persistence. Predicting 45 items on 29,715 ICU day-pairs with patient-disjoint splits, a physiology-informed gated model improves item-macro-F1 over a one-line clinical rule by +0.0019 [+0.0006,+0.0031], while losing accuracy. No macro-F1 advantage is established when the physiology window ends at the previous form's reference time (+0.0001 [-0.0006,+0.0008]), or when scoring excludes the 68.5% of cells derived from parent answers; combining both changes yields a small disadvantage. Four checkpoints across three families underperform persistence, and a fine-tuned one differs from it on only two cells. A categorical read-out raises changed-cell accuracy eightfold, but a state-only read-out scores higher overall than forecast-only decoding and matches a transition matrix. This negative result highlights how the documentation process, input cutoff, observation mask and decoding rule shape conclusions about forecasting recorded assessments.

title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
summary: Generative design of formed sheet panels must preserve geometric manufacturing conditions while exploring layouts and improving performance. STAMP embeds these conditions directly in the shape representation. Each panel is described by its material layout and a reference surface with one height at each occupied position in a plane perpendicular to the drawing direction. Nominal thickness is prescribed along the normal. The representation allows curved surfaces, ribs, and openings. It excludes reference-surface undercuts and keeps nominal thickness fixed without manufacturing penalty terms. Because these conditions belong to the representation, every generated and optimized panel satisfies them regardless of training-set size. Boundary-conditioned diffusion generates alternative layouts, and predictor gradients guide a surface optimization that retains outlines, openings, and designated fixed regions. We demonstrate STAMP on automotive hood inner panels using CarHoods10k. With a comparable number of stored values, depth maps reconstruct surfaces more accurately than point-cloud and voxel baselines. From only five training designs, one of three training runs yields novel and varied layouts. A generator trained on 500 designs, 6.5% of the training set, already reaches the layout variety of the full-data model. Across 11 held-out design families, predictor-based selection among existing dataset designs yields an average gap of 0.18 mm to the best available FEA deformation, versus an expected 1.59 mm for random selection. It does better than random selection in all 11 families. At a 10% depth-change bound, a network not used in the search predicts an average deformation reduction of 24.8% for six generated and existing panels, with a 3.2% average mass increase computed from geometry. Engineers can thus explore and optimize panels within this manufacturing-informed design space.

title: MarathonTS: a benchmark of long synthetic time series from window assembly and long-series generators
summary: Many applications of synthetic time series require a series that is much longer than the windows on which a generative model is trained. Such a series can be assembled from a pool of short generated windows, which requires deciding which windows are taken, in what order, and how their seams are processed, or it can be produced directly by a long-series generator. This study presents MarathonTS, to our knowledge the first open benchmark that compares both families under one protocol. Every method produces a series of the same length on 9 open hourly datasets with 10 seeds. The series is evaluated by its fidelity to the real data (83 metrics in 12 groups, against three real references: train, validation and an out-of-time split), by its utility (models are trained on the synthetic series only and tested on real data, TSTR against TRTR, in 14 classification and regression tasks), by its memorisation of the training data and by its computational cost. The statistical analysis is carried out as a separate stage that reads the published tables and gives the rankings of every method in every slice, the answers to the research questions with tests and uncertainty, and the results of a pre-specified confirmatory family. In the main run, the methods differ in both confirmatory cells; the choice of windows matters more than the processing of their seams, which does not improve the series, and no method trains the downstream models as well as the real series. The top tier of the leaderboard is reproduced on other hardware, whereas the exact places within it are not. For the reproducibility of the study, the code, the data hashes and all results are publicly available (links below).

title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
summary: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. Our key insight is that temporal pattern learning can benefit from abundant external time series, while spatial dependency learning remains grounded in real spatio-temporal observations. Guided by this insight, T2ST retrieves matched sequences to reinforce sparsely observed temporal patterns and selects reliable complementary sequences to broaden temporal coverage. Temporal relation distillation aligns relationships among historical patches, while multi-scale prediction distillation transfers forecasting behavior at fine and coarse temporal resolutions, enabling knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. Using only 10\% of the original spatio-temporal data, T2ST enables STFMs to achieve overall forecasting performance competitive with or superior to their full-data counterparts across six long-term and twelve short-term forecasting datasets. These results establish a new paradigm for data-efficient training of spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/T2ST-65F3/.

title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery
summary: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation. However, translating this knowledge and research experience into model designs requires preserving source context and testing applicability under task-specific assumptions. In this paper, we propose NeoResearch, a literature- and experience-guided autonomous research framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) as researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models. Specifically, NeoResearch establishes an expert-inspired dual-loop research workflow, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization through experimental feedback. To enable knowledge-grounded discovery, the agent autonomously mines scientific literature from the Web, extracting modeling mechanisms, empirical evidence, and applicability conditions to formulate task-grounded, testable architecture hypotheses. Furthermore, a hierarchical experience memory links literature findings to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons, guiding architecture discovery and training optimization while supporting reuse across forecasting tasks. Experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and support dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. Our code is available.

title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
summary: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark. It combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures to characterise benchmarks spanning a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant and to surface failure modes that task-level scores conceal. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and conduct targeted internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks, observing systematic differences in processing between knowledge-centric and reasoning-centric tasks. We shift evaluation from asking what score a model achieves toward characterising the processing patterns associated with that score, potentially supporting more targeted benchmark selection and more informed model choice. We open source our code at https://github.com/extraordinarylab/trace-kr.

title: Poetry 'resurrection' from LLMs
summary: In an era where linguistic creativity is challenged by algorithmic authorship, we pose a provocative question: can artificial intelligence (AI) write an infinite poem? We set up two experiments to investigate the quantitative and qualitative output produced by AI utilizing couplets that evidence a poetic relationship between end words, the only variation in a strict anaphoric, litany structure. Our results show that while AI can generate interesting pairings, it still falls short of human-level creativity and understanding of poetic relationships. We offer commentary and a brief survey of the field of computational poetry experiments, tracing back authorial intention and distinctions of 'natural' and 'artificial' poetry, as well as justifying why couplet form is suited to testing AI's poetic output. Experiment 1 relies on manual prompting and co-creation to extend the original poem, which is developed into an animated webpage installation and interactive artwork. Experiment 2 reliably achieves automated output reaching the 1000 benchmark via an alternative method of using an LLM in combination with semantic similarity, of which Method 2 demonstrates a higher capacity for semantic and quantitative poetic output. These experiments highlight the limitations of current LLMs' generation capacity at the word level but also suggest that poetry will also respond and revive by incorporating AI workflows.

title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation
summary: Activation steering influences a language model's behaviour by adding a steering vector to its residual stream during generation, but it requires white-box access to modify the hidden states at every generation step. We introduce ActGCG, a modification of Greedy Coordinate Gradient which optimises a suffix to match the target activations obtained by adding a steering vector to the residual stream. We further introduce universal suffixes trained across many prompts at once, a model-translation step that rewrites the suffix into human-readable text midway through optimisation, and a soft-suffix variant to remove the discrete token space constraint. We study two behaviours: steering a model to answer in German, and anti-refusal steering for jailbreaking. For German, a discrete suffix reproduces the steering vector's behaviour almost perfectly and transfers well across prompts and models. For anti-refusal, the equivalence is weaker, succeeding under a phrase-avoidance metric but only partially under the stricter HarmBench classifier. Our results show that a steering vector's behaviour is reachable from the input, with no access to model internals at generation time, up to a loss that depends on the concept being steered.

title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
summary: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. We show that what fails there is not a shortfall of accuracy but a capability in its own right -- knowing when to hold a position and when to yield to a better one -- which we call dialectical competence. It stands on first-answer accuracy without following from it: a model can be made materially better at answering and no better at this, and training for accuracy alone can drift against it. Nor can it be bought at inference, by self-reflection or by sampling more. Taking a cue from the dialectical tradition in philosophy, in which productive opposition arises within a position rather than being imposed on it from outside, we hypothesize that this capability can be trained from opposition the model supplies itself. It states a position, generates the strongest case against that position -- its antithesis -- rules on whether the case stands, and is trained on that ruling, with no second model at training or at deployment. We call this learning through Self-Disagreement: reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards throughout, where the same check that scores an answer against its reference scores the ruling too, so no reward model, no preference data and no human annotation enter anywhere. The capability is trained rather than elicited: weak in the base model, it arrives with the reward, is not paid for out of first-answer accuracy, and holds against challengers the model never trained against, including ones stronger than itself. The opposition a model needs in order to improve, it turns out, need not come from outside it.

title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
summary: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. Each item pairs premise audio and text with a hypothesis, an NLI label, and English glosses. The author assigned labels, so the dataset is an exploratory resource rather than a mature benchmark. The NLI experiments use the reference text; the audio is evaluated separately. XLM-RoBERTa baselines with five-fold item-level cross-validation reach 44.7% on Pidgin and 46.2% on Camfranglais (chance 33.3%). Still, neither is statistically distinguishable from hypothesis-only input, so hypothesis wording may account for much of the accuracy. Under disjoint-item cross-variety transfer, where a test item's counterpart is never seen in training, accuracy is 40.1% (Pidgin to Camfranglais) and 45.6% (Camfranglais to Pidgin). A counterpart-leak audit raises this to 60-64%, illustrating how counterpart leakage can overstate transfer. Zero-shot Whisper transcription of the recordings performs poorly: the best word error rates are 66.6% for Pidgin and 45.5% for Camfranglais, and with automatic language identification, Whisper Large-v3 labels 93 of 114 Pidgin recordings as Yoruba or Swahili. Together, the results suggest that such resources need disjoint-item evaluation and hypothesis-only controls, and that speech recognition must be adapted to these varieties before spoken NLI can be tested end to end.

title: Small Open-Weight Language Models for Crowd Decision-Making: Capabilities and Limits of Output-Level Fusion and Linguistic Aggregation
summary: Small open-weight language models can run crowd decision-making (CDM) on an institution's own infrastructure, which keeps the checkpoint, the inference settings and the opinions under its control. Their judgements vary across repeated queries; whether repeating and aggregating them, often through the 2-tuple linguistic representation, settles the decision rather than the labels is untested. Five open-weight models of 8-36B total parameters on one consumer GPU and a hosted reference classify 474 TripAdvisor reviews of four London restaurants ten times each; three open-weight models repeat the protocol on 600 reviews of twelve Madrid restaurants. Continuous evaluations preserve resolution: snapping each review leaves 5 distinct values against 21-65, and snapping at every level at most two collective values. Sensitivity to the participants persists once run-to-run variability is reduced: in London, redrawing the reviewers keeps the winner on 47-81% of replicas against 86-100% for redrawing the runs. With simultaneous intervals over every pair of alternatives under crowd resampling, no system on either corpus names a single winner: in London every system keeps all four restaurants as candidates, and in Madrid the candidate sets hold five to eight of the twelve. Extra runs and output-level fusion stabilize the winner but do not remove that sensitivity, and the fusion does not beat its best member. The three larger open-weight models name the hosted reference's London winner and at least match its per-review correlation with the reviewers' stars, so small open-weight models can support local CDM, reported as candidate sets with margins rather than forced rankings.

title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
summary: This research probes sentence-level semantics in massively multilingual self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) across 76 languages to understand their knowledge structure.

title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper presents a variance-reduced post-training method for Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) using a surrogate objective to address limitations of policy gradient methods.

title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
summary: GDP.xlsx is introduced as a new benchmark comprising 70 realistic workplace requests with expert rubrics and 2.18 million populated cells to evaluate frontier AI models on professional workbooks.

title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
summary: LuthorSQL is presented as a one-pass text-to-SQL model designed to act as a fast 'System 1' component for LLM agents, reducing the cost and latency of database queries while maintaining privacy.

title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
summary: RAG-FGO proposes a dynamic optimization approach for query-rewriting agents in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to address challenges like noise and hallucination in real-world deployments.

title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: CarryOn is a method for managing context in long-horizon LLM agents, learning what information to retain from interaction histories through summarization, pruning, or selection for efficient execution.

title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
summary: This study finds that large language models (LLMs), when used as reviewers, exhibit a bias towards the appendix sections of papers, influencing the reviews submitted by humans.

title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
summary: PaperCritic explores training AI reviewers to assess the soundness of academic papers, considering the multifaceted purposes of human reviewing beyond simple imitation.

title: BLiMP-RO: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Romanian
summary: BLiMP-RO is a new benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs for Romanian, designed to evaluate the grammatical knowledge of language models across 50 diverse linguistic phenomena.

title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
summary: This technical report details the fine-tuning of UltraBERT-380M encoder models with one mask per option for System One applications, comparing four recipes for scoring and probability conversion.

title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in designing geochemical experiments for real-world mineral exploration, addressing a crucial upstream capability in geoscientific automation.

title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
summary: This paper examines the trustworthiness of a shipped financial research agent, investigating its stability, diagnosing issues, and exploring auditable intervention methods beyond leaderboard scores.

title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment
summary: This research explores Human Label Variation (HLV) in textual and visual entailment, recognizing it as an informative signal that reflects diverse human interpretations of input data.

title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
summary: This paper theoretically argues that translation is both a point of origin and a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI, particularly in achieving 'world models' with internal consistency and cross-modal alignment.

title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
summary: FEND (Far-End Detection) is a new method for Voice AI agents to identify whether an outbound call is answered by a live person, voicemail, IVR, or another AI system, improving upon standard Answering Machine Detection.

title: Agent-as-a-Judge
summary: This article discusses the concept of using an 'Agent-as-a-Judge' to provide reliable evaluation, comparison, deployment insights, and post-training feedback for increasingly complex AI systems.

title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
summary: VEPO is a proposed method to mitigate multilingual hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs) by using visual evidence-guided preference optimization, particularly for low-resource languages.

title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
summary: This research demonstrates that the 'fingerprint' by which LLMs are identified is contagious, meaning a model continuing a conversation begun by another can inherit its predecessor's identity, undermining API audits.

title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
summary: Concertina is proposed as a novel approach to knowledge distillation, allowing for the direct construction of a compact student language model from the weights of a larger teacher model.

title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
summary: This paper proposes a multi-layered AI pipeline for automating the transformation of natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams. It tackles challenges like linguistic ambiguity and detecting control-flow relationships.

title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
summary: NER-D is presented as a new cross-domain benchmark for German Named Entity Recognition, comprising 13 datasets across 9 domains. It evaluates the performance of both proprietary and state-of-the-art open-source language models.

title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
summary: This paper investigates unfinished reasoning and answer recovery in clinical language models, specifically MamaReason, an adaptation of Gemma 4 31B, using MamaBench. It focuses on identifying diagnoses stated within incomplete clinical reasoning.

title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
summary: GT-FENG (General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding) is introduced as the first general framework to unify contextual factual evaluation for language models. It addresses how a model's answer correctness can vary based on specific contextual factors like jurisdiction or date.

title: Evaluating Human Sensitivity to Gender Biased AI-Generated Content through Human Assessment of Google's Autocomplete Function
summary: This study evaluates human sensitivity to gender-biased AI-generated content by examining Google's Autocomplete function. It assesses whether AI-attributed information influences the views of Spanish-speaking participants on gender-related statements, highlighting pervasive biases.

title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
summary: Gamer is introduced as a generalist vision-language-action agent framework designed for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive game environments. Its end-to-end architecture integrates perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning capabilities.

title: LitArc-Bench: Disentangling Text-Specific Reader-Response Dynamics from Position and Lexical Affect
summary: LitArc-Bench is introduced to disentangle text-specific reader-response dynamics from narrative position and lexical affect when evaluating models' tracking of human affect trajectories. It uses 39 Chinese-language literary excerpts with seven checkpoints.

title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
summary: This paper investigates whether judgments from LLM-based verifiers remain reliable when evaluating agent executions under different abstract representations. It explores the 'verification transport' issue for LLM agent evaluation when trajectories are exposed through tools or compacted histories.

title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
summary: This research explores interactive program induction, a process where a learner recovers a program from input-output examples, leveraging language model priors. This paradigm aims to broaden programming access by allowing users to demonstrate desired rule-based behavior.

title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
summary: This study investigates the use of large language model agents to automatically derive a Common Data Elements (CDE) schema from sarcoma case report abstracts. An agent successfully proposed over 70,000 candidate CDEs for information extraction at scale.

title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference
summary: Superfluid is presented as a local AI server designed for distributed Large Language Model (LLM) inference, offering benefits like data privacy, reduced costs, and low latency. It addresses deployment challenges when multiple agents or devices share a locally served model.

title: AmbiSteer: Selectively Eliciting Ambiguity-Aware Responses in Vision-Language Models
summary: AmbiSteer is a method designed to address overconfidence in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by selectively eliciting ambiguity-aware responses. It particularly focuses on cases of referential ambiguity in Visual Question Answering where visual evidence is insufficient.

title: PerfArena: Ranking LLMs by Code Performance
summary: PerfArena is introduced as a system for ranking Large Language Models (LLMs) based on their code performance, evaluating not only correctness but also time, memory, and energy costs. It addresses the need for comprehensive metrics for production-grade AI-generated code.

title: Clean Tickets, Wrong Orders: Catching Silent Errors with a Language Model in Your Browser Tab
summary: This paper describes how a small language model deployed in a browser tab can detect 'silent errors' in typed orders, where the output is syntactically correct but semantically wrong. This addresses a dangerous type of error that traditional systems often miss.

title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
summary: This paper discusses the critical point where AI judges, used to assess other systems' outputs in clinical AI, become interventions when their assessments guide prompt selection or model training. It highlights how this process can inadvertently favor errors overlooked by the judge.

title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
summary: Marimba is introduced as a System One model for speech, functioning as an interface for typed speech decisions built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features. It leverages zero-shot scoring for lexical questions and embeddings for non-lexical questions.

title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
summary: This paper envisions 'agentic robotics' as a new era in robotic systems, driven by frontier models with agentic harnesses that match or exceed task-specific policies. This paradigm shift enables robots to perform various embodied benchmarks without dedicated task training.

title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models
summary: This research applies Large Language Models (LLMs) to the challenging task of tabular anomaly detection using an f-Divergence Self-Play approach. It addresses difficulties arising from heterogeneous feature types like numerical, categorical, and textual attributes.

title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
summary: MeReader is introduced as an offline, privacy-preserving, and progress-aware AI assistant designed for narrative eBook reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional LLM systems, it processes texts locally to provide contextual companionship.

title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
summary: This paper investigates whether Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) can help explain failures in LLM-based agents, focusing on web element hallucination as a case study. It notes that MI has not yet effectively explained the decision-making processes of such agents.

title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators
summary: This paper proposes WaferTetris, a method for efficient application mapping on wafer-scale accelerators, which are hardware designed for massive compute capacity. It addresses the challenges of programming and mapping applications onto these large-scale systems.

title: ParseBench-2: Severity-Aware Evaluation of Document Parsing
summary: ParseBench-2 introduces a new method for severity-aware evaluation of document parsing, aiming to create better metrics that account for the impact of parsing errors. It addresses limitations of existing metrics that may misjudge the importance of changes.

title: Real-Time Diffusion Relighting as a Neural Sensor: Closing the Low-Light Domain Gap for Robotic Perception
summary: This research proposes using real-time diffusion relighting as a neural sensor to improve robotic perception in low-light conditions. It aims to close the domain gap for object detectors that typically fail under dark or adverse weather.

title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
summary: This study investigates adversarial attacks on image sensors used for object tracking in autonomous vehicles. It focuses on how these attacks can disrupt Tracking-By-Detection systems that estimate the motion of surrounding vehicles.

title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling
summary: This research re-examines visual reasoning within reward models used in text-to-image systems, which are crucial for prompt adherence and aesthetic judgment. It explores the prerequisites for these models to effectively bind attributes and resolve relationships.

title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
summary: This paper proposes a training-free method for accelerating multi-view 3D transformers by using regime-aware attention approximation. It addresses the quadratic cost of global attention in models that reconstruct 3D scenes from multiple images.

title: Provable Cross-Modal Transfer of Hierarchical Concept Structure in CLIP Embeddings
summary: This research provides a theoretical characterization of why CLIP embeddings exhibit hierarchical concept structure, despite not being explicitly trained for taxonomies. It explains the provable cross-modal transfer of this structure in contrastive vision-language models.

title: Open-World Scene Deocclusion
summary: This paper addresses the problem of open-world scene deocclusion, aiming to recover the complete appearance of occluded objects from a single image. It focuses on developing methods to handle clutter and complex spatial occlusions in real-world scenes.

title: RaFL: An Empirical Study of Random Filter Losses for Image Reconstruction
summary: This empirical study investigates Random Filter Losses (RaFL) for image reconstruction networks, analyzing their effectiveness compared to pixel and perceptual losses. It aims to improve the training of networks by addressing issues like averaging away fine textures.

title: HarmonyText: Harmonious Scene Text Editing via Reverse-to-Refined Pair Synthesis and Region-Decoupled Frequency Learning
summary: HarmonyText introduces a new method for natural language-guided, mask-free scene text editing in real-world images. It focuses on synthesizing refined pairs and using region-decoupled frequency learning to achieve harmonious text modifications.

title: VACO: Vertex-Aligned Decoding for Dense Hand Contact Estimation from a Single Image
summary: This research proposes VACO, a vertex-aligned decoding method for dense hand contact estimation from a single RGB image. It aims to provide a foundational primitive for dexterous manipulation and 3D interaction analysis by grounding individual vertices.

title: Efficient Genotype Classification from 3D MRI in ADPKD via Density-Aware Point Sampling and E(3)-invariance
summary: This paper presents an efficient method for genotype classification from 3D MRI scans in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) using density-aware point sampling and E(3)-invariance. The aim is to improve early detection of genetic kidney diseases.

title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
summary: This research explores how text-to-image approaches can be used for creative product design while adhering to brand image constraints. It addresses the need for creative visual exploration in industrial design.

title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
summary: This paper introduces Anisotropic Flow Models (AnisoFlow), a new approach for flow-based generative models that replaces fixed prediction targets with fully learnable ones. This method aims to improve training and sample quality by dynamically adapting the prediction target.

title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
summary: This empirical study evaluates whether large language models can optimize pretrained neural network weights through gradient-free editing, specifically in YOLO26 object detection. It assesses the generalization and value of LLM guidance for this task.

title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework designed for portable game scene generation, enabling the reuse of construction processes and experience across different game engines. It facilitates the creation of complex scenes using an orchestrated agent system.

title: Beyond Endpoints: B\'ezier Paths for Vision Foundation Model Adaptation
summary: This research investigates adapting frozen vision foundation models using B\'ezier Paths for prompt token updates, moving beyond simple endpoint adjustments. It aims to improve model adaptation as data or tasks change.

title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
summary: V-JEPA-LM describes video-language models capable of interpreting dynamic changes in scenes beyond static, text-aligned representations. These models learn scene dynamics from video and integrate with language models for question answering.

title: PADSNet: Physics-Aware Dual-Stream Network with Biomechanical Priors for Laryngeal Lesion Classification
summary: This research presents PADSNet, a physics-aware dual-stream network incorporating biomechanical priors for precise laryngeal lesion classification. It aims to improve diagnostic accuracy by leveraging both visual and vibratory dynamics.

title: DoubleTake: Focused Verification of Visual Evidence for Long-Document Understanding
summary: DoubleTake is a training-free framework designed to improve long-document understanding by enabling focused verification of visual evidence for vision-language models. It helps models identify and check specific facts more effectively during question answering.

title: Speed-Variation Distillation for Generative Modeling
summary: This paper introduces Speed-Variation Distillation, a generative framework built upon diffusion models to ensure recognizable images throughout the generation trajectory.

title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
summary: DySENSE is an AI application that synthesizes and emulates city energy data using satellite imagery to aid in achieving energy and sustainability goals.

title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
summary: This research presents an efficient AI method for predicting large-panel spatial transcriptomics directly from histology images, inferring spatially resolved gene expression profiles.

title: Zoom In, Scale Out: Metric Depth Models Mistake Digital Zoom for Moving Closer
summary: A study reveals that metric depth estimation AI models can incorrectly interpret digital zoom as a physical change in camera distance, highlighting a limitation.

title: Cracks in Embeddings: Robustness and Stability of JEPA-Based Chest X-Ray Representations
summary: This research investigates the robustness and stability of JEPA-based self-supervised models when applied to chest X-ray representations in medical imaging.

title: CardioTrace: Motion-Aware Cine Synthesis via Coupled Tracing and Segmentation
summary: CardioTrace introduces an AI method for motion-aware cardiac cine synthesis, enabling improved visualization even with sparse or degraded MRI sequences.

title: Vessel2Brain: Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Flow Matching for 3D Brain Image Generation from Vessel Masks
summary: Vessel2Brain presents an AI method using multi-scale flow matching for generating realistic 3D brain MRI volumes from sparse anatomical priors like vessel masks.

title: Token2Tile: Token-Wise Sparse Attention with Tile Execution through a Low-Rank Space for Video DiTs
summary: Token2Tile proposes a method for efficient video diffusion transformers, utilizing token-wise sparse attention with tile execution through a low-rank space.

title: Domain Adaptation Based Pipeline for Character Classification and Handwritten Text Recognition
summary: This paper proposes a novel unsupervised domain adaptation pipeline for character classification and handwritten text recognition, addressing challenges with limited labeled data.

title: nnAEU: a Simple and Efficient CNN-Autoencoder for Hyperspectral Unmixing
summary: nnAEU introduces a simple and efficient CNN-Autoencoder designed for hyperspectral unmixing, offering an alternative to more complex deep learning architectures.

title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
summary: In this paper, a new real-world benchmark is introduced for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction directly on handwritten essay images, focusing on grounded edits.

title: RSSA: Robust Semantic and Spatial Aligner for Collaborative Perception
summary: RSSA introduces a Robust Semantic and Spatial Aligner designed to improve collaborative perception in V2X systems by accurately aligning multi-view features.

title: JaRS: Contrast-Free Localization of Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Jacobian Row Sums
summary: JaRS proposes a contrast-free method to localize memorized regions within diffusion models using Jacobian Row Sums, helping to address privacy and copyright concerns.

title: Multi-level latent-diffusion adaptation for cross-region point cloud segmentation of ancient terraces
summary: This research explores multi-level latent-diffusion adaptation for cross-region point cloud segmentation, specifically for archaeological surveys of ancient terraces.

title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation
summary: InfiHall-Bench is presented as a new benchmark for evaluating hallucination in autoregressive text-to-image generation models, addressing limitations of existing diffusion-centric benchmarks.

title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
summary: SWAM introduces a Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging method to enhance the efficiency of Vision Transformers by reducing their computational costs through token reduction.

title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
summary: TelePhysica explores agentic reconstruction of physically interactive scenes, aiming to overcome limitations in current image-to-video diffusion models and 3D reconstruction techniques.

title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
summary: EcoVGGT introduces a method for efficient and streamable feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos, improving multi-view transformers by addressing quadratic cost issues.

title: KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models
summary: KnowVis presents a dual-view evaluation and diagnosis method for assessing how well text-to-image models ground world-knowledge in their generations.

title: DRA-HTR: Disentangling Representation and Adaptation for Handwritten Text Recognition
summary: DRA-HTR proposes a method to disentangle representation and adaptation, addressing challenges in Handwritten Text Recognition, especially for historical documents.

title: STaG: Human-Annotation-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Text-Based Person Retrieval
summary: STaG is a new method for human-annotation-free unsupervised domain adaptation in text-based person retrieval, addressing the bottleneck of missing textual annotations in new domains.

title: SCAR: Bridging Coarse Retrieval and Fine Localization through Candidate Reranking
summary: SCAR is a method that improves natural-language point-cloud localization by reranking candidates, addressing how the final output is currently determined by retrieval order rather than coordinate relevance.

title: Lens: Training-Free Semantic Search for Cross-Tile Object and Scene Retrieval in Satellite Imagery
summary: Lens is a training-free system for semantic object and scene search across large satellite mosaics, utilizing a frozen, self-supervised vision transformer without needing a detector trained for specific classes.

title: Deep Bundle Adjustment
summary: DeepBA is a graph neural network designed to recover camera poses, intrinsics, and scene structure from 2D matches across multiple views, amortizing the traditional non-linear least-squares problem.

title: Structural Self-Teaching for Compositional Generation in Unified Multimodal Models
summary: Structural Self-Teaching (SST) is a novel framework that enhances compositional image generation in diffusion-based unified multimodal models by using their internal understanding path for structural supervision.

title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation
summary: This paper presents a weakly supervised approach for video semantic segmentation (WS-VSS) that aims to unlock cross-attention mechanisms for learning temporal relationships under label-scarce conditions.

title: DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis
summary: DIRT is a method for live novel-view synthesis that uses depth-completed image-based rendering and two-band blending to achieve low-latency rendering and strong generalization in new scenes.

title: MaskSCD: Bitemporal Mask Classification for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
summary: MaskSCD is a method for semantic change detection in remote sensing images that uses bitemporal mask classification to identify land surface changes and the specific land-cover transitions.

title: Agentic-Teacher: An Agentic Data Engine for Failure-Driven VLA Post-Training
summary: Agentic-Teacher is an agentic data engine designed for failure-driven post-training of vision-language-action (VLA) models, where agents autonomously generate demonstrations to address model weaknesses.

title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
summary: This research focuses on teaching Vision-Language-Navigation (VLN) models to perform budget-conditioned object search, enabling them to adapt their exploration strategy based on varying time constraints.

title: Learning Latent Goal Costs for Visual World-Model Planning with an Expanding Curriculum
summary: This paper explores learning latent goal costs for visual world-model planning, focusing on how predicted observations are scored against a goal in image-goal planning to overcome visual similarities across obstacles.

title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
summary: This paper introduces a synthetic multi-turn dialogue benchmark for human intent extraction and action planning in robotics, addressing challenges in conversational human-robot interaction.

title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety
summary: This paper presents a framework using vision-language models (VLMs) to infer task- and scene-dependent safety constraints for robots by grounding object-to-object hazard reasoning into 3D risk fields.

title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
summary: This technical report details X-Nav, a system enabling real-world long-horizon indoor-to-outdoor navigation on a humanoid robot, addressing challenges like complex instructions and camera movement.

title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks
summary: This research investigates the utility of pre-trained visual representations for policy learning in visuomotor imitation learning, aiming to improve data efficiency and robustness for contact-rich robotic insertion tasks.

title: AI-guided robotic in situ fabrication of curvature- and tissue-adaptive wireless bioelectronics
summary: This paper presents an AI-guided robotic in situ printing platform for fabricating curvature- and tissue-adaptive wireless bioelectronic devices that can conform to complex body surfaces and adjust electrical characteristics.

title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost
summary: This research shows how imitation policies for robot manipulation learn to discount noisy object positions, revealing that the robot's own state acts as a proprioceptive anchor to provide information about object location.

title: EViDS: An Environment--Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Simulation Platform for Intelligent Chassis Development
summary: EViDS is a simulation platform integrating environmental and perception information with high-fidelity vehicle dynamics, designed to support the development of intelligent chassis for autonomous vehicles.

title: Ego2Flow: Benchmarking the Traffic-System Impact of Autonomous Driving on Maps Distilled from Real-World Roads
summary: Ego2Flow is a closed-loop benchmark designed to evaluate the collective traffic-system impact of autonomous driving, moving beyond single-vehicle safety and task completion.

title: ERA: Error-Resistant Autonomous Object Navigation with Predicted Depth
summary: ERA is a method for error-resistant autonomous object navigation that utilizes predicted depth from RGB images, enabling zero-shot navigation without a dedicated depth sensor.

title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
summary: This research paper explores how cross-view consistency in multi-view appearance augmentation affects visuomotor policies in controlled simulation studies.

title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions
summary: This paper presents a multimodal person concept model designed to improve person identification for service robots in domestic and office environments under varying observation conditions.

title: Reusing Locomotion Training Recipes Across Humanoids via Body-Aligned Virtual Joints
summary: This research focuses on a method for reusing reinforcement learning training recipes for humanoid locomotion across different humanoid robots by using body-aligned virtual joints.

title: A Generalizable Approach to Safety-Aware Robotic Behavior Planning with an Explicit Constraint Space
summary: This paper introduces a generalizable approach to safety-aware robotic behavior planning, addressing challenges in safe manipulation in tabletop environments using large language and vision-language models.

title: PoliMop: Policy-in-the-Loop Motion Planning in 3D Spaces for Mobile Robots
summary: This paper presents PoliMop, a policy-in-the-loop motion planning method for mobile robots to navigate complex 3D environments with challenging terrain and obstacles.

title: Evaluating Language Models as Spatial Priors for Object-Goal Navigation
summary: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in providing spatial priors for object-goal navigation tasks, moving beyond semantic association scores.

title: ESI: An Embodied Self-Improvement Flywheel for LLM-VLA Agents
summary: This paper proposes ESI, an embodied self-improvement mechanism for LLM-VLA agents to achieve coordinated behavior by addressing divergences between LLM intentions and VLA actions.

title: NPU-Accelerated GNSS Signal Acquisition
summary: This paper proposes using the Neural Processing Unit (NPU) on small single-board computers as an accelerator for GNSS signal acquisition, rather than for machine learning tasks, to reduce CPU load.

title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: This paper explores the use of vision-language model cost programs, connecting VLMs with model-predictive controllers for contact-rich manipulation tasks in 3D environments.

title: PROOF: Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion
summary: This research introduces PROOF, a method for improving the perceptive robustness of vision-based legged locomotion for robots by using an out-of-distribution fallback mechanism.

title: Heavy Metal Acrobatics: Learning Dynamic Control for Skid-Steer Loaders
summary: This paper investigates methods for learning dynamic control for skid-steer loaders, aiming to automate heavy machinery in industries like construction and mining.

title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
summary: This is a life-cycle survey of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, covering their design, training, and deployment for generating robot actions by adapting web-pretrained models.

title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
summary: This paper investigates the hardware implementation of linear-attention language models on edge FPGAs, specifically addressing the cost of memory paging for recurrent states from RTL to silicon.

title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
summary: This structured scoping review examines the evolution from AI-enabled remote patient monitoring to agentic AI systems in healthcare, focusing on embodiment, governance, and care integration.

title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
summary: This research improves the robustness of self-play trained humanoid robots for object handover with unfamiliar partners by introducing a hidden start delay in the policy.

title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
summary: This research explores how telerobotic interventions can improve the resilience of self-driving laboratories (SDLs), which integrate robotics and AI for automated experimentation in scientific research.

title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
summary: This paper focuses on accurately modeling frictional contact for continuum robots with their environments using a Linear Complementarity Problem approach, essential for precise motion control.

title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
summary: This research explores methods for training Robot-use agents (RUAs) in simulation to enable them to natively and effectively control real robots for general-purpose tasks.

title: CS-MPC: Contraction-Certified Sampling-Based MPC for Nonlinear Systems Under Uncertainty
summary: This paper presents CS-MPC, a contraction-certified sampling-based model predictive control method for ensuring tracking and safety of nonlinear robotic systems under uncertainty.

title: Foundation Model Driven Robotics: A Comprehensive Review
summary: This is a comprehensive review examining the transformative impact of foundation models, such as large language and vision-language models, on the field of robotics.

title: E0: Expressive Fine-Grained Discrete Action Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models via Tweedie Discrete Diffusion
summary: This item describes a method for expressive fine-grained discrete action prediction using Tweedie discrete diffusion, enhancing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation.

title: Long-Distance Real-World Navigation of the Legged-Wheeled Robot Go2-W Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper reports on the long-distance, real-world navigation capabilities of the legged-wheeled robot Go2-W, utilizing deep reinforcement learning for autonomous movement.

title: The Missing Touch: Sensing and Displaying Localized Contact Geometry Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
summary: This research explores improving robotic teleoperation dexterity by sensing and displaying localized contact geometry, aiming for more intuitive control of remote robots.

title: Fast Non-Parametric Heteroscedastic Imitation Learning With Geometric Priors
summary: This paper introduces a method for fast non-parametric heteroscedastic imitation learning, utilizing geometric priors to efficiently learn probabilistic policies from human demonstrations.

title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination
summary: This item presents PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework enabling two humanoid robots to play table tennis doubles with agile movements and safe team coordination in a shared space.

title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation
summary: This research introduces IORA, a method for immobilizing irregular objects during robotic manipulation, specifically addressing stable grasping with low-degrees-of-freedom hands under restricted actuation.

title: OneSteer: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
summary: This paper introduces OneSteer, a one-step diffusion whole-body controller that enables steerable general humanoid motion tracking by combining motion tracking with selective test-time steering.

title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces VOKE (Visual Object Kinematics Estimator), a system designed to estimate object movement for dexterous in-hand manipulation, going beyond static object poses.

title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
summary: This paper introduces HEIR, a resource for studying human-robot interactions by enabling robots to interpret human egocentric intent and execute complex tasks involving navigation and manipulation.

title: Beyond Trajectory Similarity: Evaluating Surgical Planning by Protocol Adherence
summary: This research proposes evaluating surgical planning based on protocol adherence rather than just trajectory similarity, aiming to improve assessment of task completion in healthcare applications.

title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This paper introduces D-VLA, a high-concurrency distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework designed to address systemic bottlenecks when training large Vision-Language-Action models in distributed environments.

title: Self-Building Labs
summary: This item describes 'Self-Building Labs,' an application of AI agents to automate experimental execution, optimization, and adaptation for accelerated scientific discovery.

title: A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks
summary: This abstract discusses auditing short-clip pose benchmarks, highlighting issues with how vision benchmarks align predictions to ground truth before scoring.

title: Geometric Refinement and Distributional Alignment for Sim2Real Roadside LiDAR Detection
summary: This item describes an approach using geometric refinement and distributional alignment for a Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, focusing on training 3D object detectors with synthetic data for roadside detection.

title: Coordinate Frame Recovery, Per Class NMS and Null Return Modelling for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection
summary: This item describes an approach to the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, focusing on methods like coordinate frame recovery and null return modeling for V2X LiDAR detection using synthetic data.

title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
