summary: This paper introduces a recoverability-aware curriculum for super-resolution in smart-glasses images, improving VLM performance for visual assistance by addressing image degradations.

title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
summary: This research focuses on automatically extracting structured powder X-ray diffraction data from images in scientific publications, specifically for covalent organic frameworks.

title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
summary: MoMoVL proposes a modality-aware adaptive compression method for on-device sparsely-activated Vision-Language Models, aiming to enhance privacy and reduce latency for cross-modal web tasks.

title: What Do Learned 3D Models Add to Localization from Posed References?
summary: This research investigates the contribution of learned 3D models to localization from posed reference images, comparing their camera predictions against geometric estimation across various models and datasets.

title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework
summary: This comprehensive study examines the deployment of computer vision on edge devices, proposing a unified hardware-model-runtime mapping framework to address architectural heterogeneity.

title: CoScan: Multi-Scale Content-Adaptive Space-Filling Scans for Causal State-Space Image Restoration
summary: CoScan introduces multi-scale, content-adaptive space-filling scans for causal state-space image restoration, addressing the challenge of linearizing 2D feature maps for efficient processing.

title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
summary: This research probes whether 3D point representations, from both supervised and pretrained models, encode architectural functions of building elements on urban facades, beyond mere semantic labels.

title: GaussLearner: 3D Gaussian Primitives as Self-Regulating Continual Learners
summary: GaussLearner proposes using 3D Gaussian primitives as self-regulating continual learners to maintain faithful reconstructions of evolving 3D environments, addressing catastrophic forgetting.

title: Detect What You Need: Chain-of-Causal Reasoning for 3D Intent Grounding
summary: This paper introduces Chain-of-Causal Reasoning for 3D Intent Grounding (3D-IG), aiming to accurately localize target 3D objects in 3D space based on natural-language intentions.

title: GramStatTexNet: Efficient, Interpretable, and Neuro-Inspired Texture Analysis-by-Synthesis
summary: GramStatTexNet is an efficient, interpretable, and neuro-inspired model for texture analysis-by-synthesis that aims to combine the realism of deep networks with the interpretability of neuroscience-informed models.

title: Keep the Reasoning, Read the Image: On-Demand Visual KV for Multi-Turn Reasoning VLMs
summary: This research introduces a method for on-demand visual KV caching in multi-turn reasoning Vision-Language Models to better retain image information, addressing issues with KV cache pruning.

title: DetectViT: Test-time Backdoor Detection for Vision Transformers via Inter-Head Attention Discrepancy
summary: DetectViT proposes a test-time backdoor detection method for Vision Transformers by analyzing inter-head attention discrepancy, aiming to secure models that use third-party pretrained checkpoints.

title: ROBIN++: Unified Copyright Protection and Tamper Localization for Diffusion Models via Dual-Domain Synergistic Watermarking
summary: ROBIN++ introduces a unified dual-domain synergistic watermarking method for diffusion models, providing both copyright protection and tamper localization for generated content.

title: Sightline: Long-Window Speculative Decoding for Fast SVG Generation
summary: Sightline introduces long-window speculative decoding for fast SVG generation models, aiming to speed up the drawing process by allowing the model to guess and verify many tokens per pass.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
summary: This research introduces PReMind, a vision-language assistant that uses personal memories and context to provide tailored advice, especially when identifying visual hazards.

title: SWIFT: Slow World, Instant Freshness, and Timely Action for Asynchronous Autonomous Driving
summary: SWIFT is a system designed to improve real-time world-action planning and control in asynchronous autonomous driving by maintaining observation freshness.

title: TOGBench: Benchmarking and Improving Tiny-Object Generation Fidelity in Aerial Imagery
summary: TOGBench is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating and improving the fidelity of deep generative models in synthesizing tiny objects within aerial imagery.

title: ReflectScene:MLLM-Guided Closed-Loop Diffusion for 3D Indoor Scene Generation
summary: ReflectScene proposes an MLLM-guided, closed-loop diffusion method for text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation, addressing limitations of static textual conditions.

title: Temporal Image Representations for Mouse Dynamics Authentication
summary: This research explores using temporal image representations and computer vision models for mouse dynamics authentication, moving beyond traditional handcrafted features.

title: Grounding Radiology Reports in 3D Chest CT: Results of the ReXGrounding Challenge
summary: The ReXGrounding Challenge is presented to advance the task of grounding radiology reports in 3D Chest CT scans by segmenting and tracking reported findings.

title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive expert orchestration method for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) to help MLLMs adapt to new data while retaining prior knowledge.

title: Keep the Image in Mind: A Visual Board for Multimodal Agents
summary: This paper introduces a 'Visual Board' mechanism for multimodal agents to better represent and retain visual evidence, improving multi-step visual reasoning and preventing misinterpretations.

title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
summary: NullTok is a new training-free token selection method designed to improve long video understanding for multimodal large language models by efficiently handling numerous visual tokens.

title: Can AI Understand Indonesian Children's Book Illustrations? Compliance, Safety, and the Cultural Alignment Gap
summary: This paper examines whether AI systems can understand Indonesian children's book illustrations, raising questions about compliance, safety, and cultural alignment gaps when AI enters publishing.

title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning
summary: SixthView is introduced as a new benchmark for models to predict hidden views and reason about 3D assembly, particularly in scenarios of part placement and occlusion.

title: ProxySearch: Decoupled Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Asymmetric Noise-Rank Transfer
summary: ProxySearch is a method to decouple inference-time scaling for text-to-image diffusion models, improving noise search efficiency using asymmetric noise-rank transfer.

title: TRoPE: Topology-aware Relative Positional Encoding for 4D Generation
summary: TRoPE introduces Topology-aware Relative Positional Encoding to improve video-to-4D mesh generation, addressing issues like sticking artifacts in dynamic 3D geometry recovery.

title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
summary: BiCAT introduces Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization to enable autoregressive vision-language-action models to perform bimanual manipulation with robots.

title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
summary: TAG is a new compact, low-cost robotic platform developed for studying learning and control within physically coupled dynamical systems, demonstrated with a ball-in-maze and inverted pendulum.

title: RageVLA: Augmentation-Trained Perception and Action for State-of-the-Art Robustness on LIBERO
summary: RageVLA presents an augmentation-trained perception and action framework for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing robustness in robotic manipulation tasks like those in LIBERO.

title: Learning the Dynamics of Deformable Linear Objects Through Coupled Oscillators for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research explores a learning-based approach using coupled oscillators to understand the dynamics of deformable linear objects, improving bimanual robotic manipulation.

title: LuxTac: A Flexible, Scalable, and Open-Source Optical Taxel Array with Distributed Three-Axis Force Sensing for Tactile Robot Learning
summary: LuxTac is presented as a flexible, scalable, and open-source optical taxel array with three-axis force sensing, designed as a practical tactile input for robot learning.

title: SPICE: Stochastic Policy for Interaction in Cluttered Environments
summary: SPICE is a stochastic policy developed for robots to perform agricultural tasks in cluttered environments, focusing on learning contact-responsive behaviors amidst obstructed vision.

title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
summary: This paper discusses a new paradigm for certified safety in robotics, advocating for 'Recoverability, Not Invariance' to ensure robots' performance at their operational limits.

title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models
summary: This research proposes a visual planner for robots that combines a frozen latent world model with sampling-based model predictive control, enabling self-correction for discrepancies between commanded and executed actions.

title: LoRN: Low-Rank Noise Steering for Generative Robot Policies
summary: This paper introduces Low-Rank Noise Steering (LoRN) to improve pretrained generative robot policies by learning to select initial noise inputs without updating model weights, leveraging the sensitivity of actions to video noise.

title: Radar-Native Control Barrier Functions: Doppler Range Rate as a Measured Barrier Derivative
summary: This research proposes using Doppler range rate directly from radar measurements as a barrier derivative for control barrier functions, aiming to improve safe control around dynamic obstacles by avoiding delays and noise sensitivity from traditional range-based filters.

title: Finetuning VLAs for Dexterous Manipulation: The Right Checkpoint Is All You Need
summary: This paper investigates fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for dexterous manipulation, highlighting the challenge of transferring capabilities from parallel-jaw grippers to multi-finger hands due to dataset limitations.

title: ExecGap: Exploiting Command-Execution Gap for Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research introduces ExecGap, a method for patch attacks on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models controlling robots, exploiting the command-execution gap to compromise reliable robot operation.

title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data
summary: This paper proposes a method for improving deployed end-to-end driving models by learning proactively from imperfect human takeover data, addressing issues like late or unnecessary interventions.

title: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies
summary: This research introduces RecallFlow, which uses episodic memory as the source distribution for generative robot policies to enable memory-dependent manipulation, allowing robots to act on information no longer visible.

title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability
summary: This paper investigates how priors acquired by video generation models can be effectively used to bridge the gap between predictive power and policy learnability for robots manipulating unfamiliar objects.

title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
summary: This research introduces CoT-WAM, a method for collaboratively training Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via plan latents to improve general robot manipulation by enhancing semantic competence and physical foresight.

title: RoboDx: Repair and Diagnosis of Faults in Robot Software
summary: This paper introduces RoboDx, a system designed to generate repair tasks for simulated robots, focusing on diagnosing and fixing faults in robot navigation software that traditional unit tests might miss.

title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research presents RePlan-VLA, a progress-aware replanning framework designed to improve the performance of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models on long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks that involve multiple interdependent steps.

title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
summary: This paper introduces LAGR (Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking), a method that improves task-oriented robotic grasping by re-ranking potential grasps based on both physical criteria and language-derived task context.

title: Navigating Robots from Unknown and Uncalibrated Exocentric Cameras via Map Estimation
summary: This research proposes a method for navigating robots using unknown and uncalibrated exocentric cameras by estimating a map, leveraging wider vantage points for improved perception in indoor environments.

title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors
summary: This paper presents ReLoco, a framework that unifies humanoid locomotion and fall recovery by learning a single policy using behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors, enabling robots to sustain motion despite falls.

title: GTI: Grounding Task Intent Throughout Long-Horizon VLA Manipulation
summary: This research proposes GTI (Grounding Task Intent), a method for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to maintain global task intent throughout long-horizon robotic manipulation by grounding it in the current executable context.

title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
summary: This paper presents a hierarchical onboard vision-language-navigation framework designed for aerial robots (UAVs) to achieve semantic reasoning and long-horizon navigation in complex environments under strict onboard constraints.

title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
summary: This research introduces Emo-H2A, a system that drives a facial robot's expressions directly from Large Language Model (LLM) hidden states at token rate, aiming for diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions in human-robot interaction.

title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: This paper presents 3DTouch, a tactile-aware Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that integrates 3D geometric relations to enhance dexterous manipulation, particularly in contact-rich scenarios where visual occlusion is problematic.

title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
summary: This research introduces CoRA-VTLA, a method that employs contact-guided attention and queryable response memory for tactile post-training, enabling Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to perform precision manipulation tasks with essential contact feedback.

title: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning
summary: This paper presents LaST1.0, a unified latent world-action model that focuses on control-centric spatio-temporal reasoning to enhance robotic policies by more effectively capturing environmental dynamics for robust control.

title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
summary: This research introduces a new policy using World Action Models for arm-free quadrupedal robots to perform loco-manipulation, allowing them to walk on three legs while manipulating with a front leg following language instructions.

title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
summary: This research presents SemPhys, a semantic-physical co-learning approach using differentiable world models to generate humanoid robot whole-body movements from natural language instructions in human-robot collaboration.

title: Meaning Reaches Object Choice but Not Completion: Where Is a VLA Vulnerable to Landmark Synonyms?
summary: This study investigates the vulnerability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, specifically GR00T N1.7, to rewording and landmark synonyms in robot manipulation tasks, analyzing whether failure occurs in object choice or task completion.

title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
summary: This research explores cross-model action misalignment in commercial embodied robots that use large language models to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction.

title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
summary: This research introduces Ego2X, a method for contact-aware transfer of egocentric human interaction data to any robot, aiming to overcome the challenges of collecting real interaction data on physical robots.

title: Assessing Vision-Language Models for Early Prediction of Unsafe Situations in Robotics
summary: This research assesses the capability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to predict unsafe situations and potential failures in robotics early, addressing the limited evidence for their effectiveness in this domain.

title: BEV-Diffusion: Camera-Only Traversability Navigation with BEV Memory and Efficient Cross-Robot Adaptation
summary: This research introduces BEV-Diffusion, a camera-only model that learns a bird's-eye view traversability map for efficient robot navigation and cross-robot adaptation, aiming to reduce reliance on expensive LiDAR sensors.

title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
summary: This research proposes efficient world-model planning via physics-guided search distillation to support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories and ensuring road-compliant execution.

title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
summary: This research introduces constrained world-model planning for visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring, focusing on efficiently localizing multiple targets under compute and sensing constraints.

title: High-Precision Docking of Differential-Drive Mobile Robots Through LiDAR and Vision Collaboration
summary: This research proposes a method for high-precision docking of differential-drive mobile robots by combining global navigation with terminal control, using complementary LiDAR and visual observations.

title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
summary: This research introduces TapTacTouch, a vision-free and training-free method for 3D object shape completion using sparse tactile contacts, designed for robotic perception and manipulation where visual observations are limited.

title: Neural Network-Based In-Contact Task Segmentation of Demonstrated Robot Motions via Hand Guiding
summary: This research proposes a neural network-based method for in-contact task segmentation of demonstrated robot motions via hand guiding, improving programming by demonstration for tasks requiring force control.

title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning
summary: This research introduces ProbeShare for fast world-model planning, enabling efficient visual planning with a frozen joint-embedding world model to support robotic reaching and object manipulation by evaluating action sequences.

title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning
summary: This research presents CommDreamer, utilizing radio-geometric world models for mapless trajectory planning of cellular-connected unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to ensure reliable connectivity and collision-free flight in complex urban environments.

title: Towards Vacuum-Assisted Robotic Needle Interventions: From Fluid Aspiration to Tissue Biopsy
summary: This research explores vacuum-assisted robotic needle interventions, focusing on improving the acquisition of diagnostic material through fluid aspiration and tissue biopsy, beyond just target localization and needle placement.

title: Old Experience, New Lessons: Relabeling Autonomous Robot Rollouts in Interactive Imitation Learning
summary: This research proposes relabeling autonomous robot rollouts within interactive imitation learning to leverage sparse human corrections and abundant robot experience for improved task learning.

title: QDD-MM: A Simple and Compact Open-Source Muscle Module with Quasi-Direct-Drive Motor for Tendon-driven Robots
summary: This introduces QDD-MM, a simple and compact open-source muscle module featuring a quasi-direct-drive motor designed for tendon-driven robots, offering benefits like variable stiffness and redundant actuation.

title: Remote Teleoperation of Endovascular Robots: A Network Emulation Framework for Systematic Performance Evaluation
summary: This research presents a network emulation framework for systematically evaluating the performance of remote teleoperation for endovascular robots, focusing on the effects of network degradation on usability in clinical settings.

title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
summary: A new theory of software thermodynamics is introduced to analyze token usage, heat, entropy, and error in agentic coding systems, drawing parallels from classical thermodynamics.

title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
summary: This paper presents HardwareDx, a graph model system designed to improve datacenter machine repairs, crucial for maintaining the reliability of AI infrastructure and minimizing economic losses from hardware failures.

title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
summary: RFBench is introduced as a new simulator-grounded multimodal benchmark and dataset designed to evaluate the ability of language models to understand and design passive radio-frequency layouts.

title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
summary: LusoClin is a new synthetic clinical note dataset created to advance medical information retrieval research in European Portuguese, addressing the scarcity of real clinical data due to privacy concerns.

title: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
summary: VeriMath proposes a human-in-the-loop system for generating and verifying curriculum-aligned mathematics assessment items, tackling challenges in automated educational content creation.

title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
summary: This paper introduces GUARD, a method using regret guidance to stabilize the recursive self-improvement process in autonomous AI agents, addressing issues where self-editing often backfires.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
summary: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and image navigation behavior of vision-language model agents when reading emergency CT and MRI examinations. It studies how different exploration strategies affect agent performance in medical imaging tasks.

title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
summary: Introduces SpecLook, a method to improve the speed and reliability of agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by speculating where to look during zoom-in tool calls. This aims to reduce the slowness of sequential reasoning loops in MLLMs.

title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
summary: Explores the phenomenon of attention sinks in large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs), where the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token receives a disproportionate share of attention. It investigates how this affects model behavior under standard causal masking.

title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
summary: Introduces GRAFT, a method for automated agent design that uses execution-guided genetic recombination to improve LLM-based agent performance. It focuses on evolving executable architectures for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification.

title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
summary: Presents BeFit, a method that shifts complexity from neural network weights to Bernstein activations, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers for time-series sensing. This approach aims to maintain accuracy while reducing computational demands.

title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
summary: Introduces FACET, a method for estimating Big Five personality traits from life narratives using facet-aware contrastive embeddings. It aims to improve personality prediction from text by combining language-model and psycholinguistic representations.

title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
summary: Introduces LProp, a method for LLM agents to propagate latent uncertainty through evidence-conditioned belief revision. It aims to ensure that tentative assumptions are not treated as facts in downstream decisions by preserving and updating inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives.

title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance
summary: Discusses a multi-agent system designed to provide receiver-conditioned clarification for food assistance, helping households find usable food resources. This guidance connects eligibility requirements, access constraints, and dietary needs for personalized recommendations.

title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
summary: Proposes ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical self-evolving memory architecture for enterprise LLM agents. This memory system is designed to maintain accuracy and cost-efficiency in dynamic environments with evolving foundation models and workflows.

title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
summary: Explores multi-objective retrieval strategies for heterogeneous scientific modalities, particularly in cosmology, where observational datasets have uneven coverage. It compares approaches using multimodal foundation models and independently learned modality embeddings to address this challenge.

title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
summary: Discusses evaluating autonomous agents that run ML experiments, focusing on metrics beyond the final score, such as adherence to allowed edits, provenance of decisions, and handling of failed trials. It aims to assess the agent's entire experimentation lifecycle.

title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
summary: Introduces KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool designed to help researchers identify promising new papers from a growing volume of similar work. It combines multiple sources of evidence to generate personalized reading priorities.

title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
summary: Studies the temporal structure and dynamics of language-model reasoning, analyzing how LLMs alternate between sustained activities and local operations. It introduces T/E/S to combine text, local events, and activity spans to predict continuation and analyze computational needs.

title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
summary: Proposes a universal System-1 model to handle common decision points across various autonomous LLM agent workflows, reducing cost and latency. This approach aims to replace workflow-specific System-1 models with a single, generalizable solution.

title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
summary: Addresses the challenge of continually extending the tool space of multimodal agents by efficiently integrating new specialist vision models. The research focuses on enabling agents to learn and utilize new tools without disrupting existing capabilities.

title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
summary: Introduces "metrics-in-the-loop" to provide coding agents with inference-time feedback on code complexity and test coverage. This aims to guide agents to write better code by addressing issues that passing tests alone do not reveal.

title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
summary: Proposes an evidence-based credit assignment method for reinforcement learning in search-augmented language models. This technique assigns credit based on the utility of retrieved information, rather than uniform credit for every search in a trajectory.

title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
summary: Presents a System 1 decision model for medical multiple-choice questions, built upon frozen language models. This model processes questions and options into vectors, using trained heads to identify the closest correct answer in a shared space.

title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
summary: Introduces RoboBuilder, a benchmark where AI agents co-design robot hardware and programs using standard and 3D-printed parts, with real-world video feedback. It evaluates whether coding agents can design functional robots tested on physical courses after simulation.

title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
summary: Investigates the challenge of decision coverage in natural-language data querying, where large language models translate questions into executable programs. The study focuses on recognizing multiple computational interpretations and identifying decisions needed to resolve them.

title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
summary: Describes a method for risk-controlled correction in deployed multimodal models when some input modalities are missing, addressing how to fix errors in frozen models.

title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
summary: Introduces EVA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement method for video evaluators to better identify motion defects and improve the temporal quality of generated videos.

title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
summary: Investigates the effectiveness of evaluation methods for invariance training in neural graph algorithms, specifically questioning if current metrics detect lost sensitivity to answer-changing input edits.

title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
summary: Presents a method for training-free domain generation to improve one-shot federated learning with server-side pre-trained diffusion models, addressing challenges with heterogeneous client distributions.

title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
summary: Introduces MLE Agents, autonomous AI agents designed to streamline and automate the machine learning engineering workflow for improving large-scale recommendation systems.

title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
summary: Develops MyoECG, a cross-modal representation learning system that uses cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography for biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection.

title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
summary: Explores methods to make LLMs believe false facts within prompts, aiming to improve alignment evaluations without requiring new model finetuning for each false belief.

title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
summary: Introduces GLIDE, a scalable and event-aware system for inductive forecasting of order volumes over evolving logistics graphs, specifically for on-demand food delivery platforms.

title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
summary: Presents SCAFFOLD, a framework aiming to ensure warrant-preserving evidence transport for reusable LLM-agent skills, addressing challenges in maintaining justification and reliability over time.

title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains
summary: Introduces Space-X, a system of self-evolving spatial agents designed to improve spatial reasoning by effectively weaving visual, geometric, and linguistic clues into coherent evidence chains.

title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
summary: Discusses Test-Time Symmetrization and scaling laws for model-agnostic learning, focusing on how test-time compute can improve language model accuracy during inference.

title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
summary: Proposes a capability framework for evaluating agentic AI platforms in regulated enterprises, highlighting limitations of existing public agent benchmarks in assessing integrated systems.

title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
summary: Challenges the causal interpretation of attention mechanisms in AI models, questioning their ability to accurately represent the relevance of objects and interpret autonomous vehicle driving decisions.

title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
summary: Introduces the 3D GameDev Arena for benchmarking coding agents on their ability to plan, build, and playtest complex 3D browser games, highlighting the challenges of evaluating long-horizon tasks.

title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
summary: Presents a method for recurrent domain incremental adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to enable continuous improvement under changing operating conditions without sacrificing prior knowledge.

title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
summary: Proposes fast Bayesian methods for uncertainty quantification in sparse AI evaluation, enabling efficient estimation of AI system performance on new benchmarks with limited outcomes.

title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
summary: Introduces GALA, a method for gallery-level alignment to improve the real-life vision decoding from EEG signals, particularly addressing generalization across individuals.

title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
summary: Proposes an LLM-guided workflow evolution approach for token-efficient automated red teaming, leveraging multi-agent systems to identify safety failures in large language models.

title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
summary: Explores rethinking multimodal alignment to enable physical AI systems to understand real-world mechanics and physical events, moving beyond static object recognition to dynamic trajectories.

title: FedE2E: One-Shot Federated Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Closed-Loop Evaluation
summary: Introduces FedE2E, a one-shot federated learning method designed for end-to-end autonomous driving that incorporates closed-loop evaluation to overcome communication overhead and perception task limitations.

title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces an "agentic orchestra" framework for computer-aided music composition and performance using quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. Musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error engagement within a musical environment.

title: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs
summary: This paper explores agentic knowledge engineering, where LLM agents transform raw data into reasoning-ready knowledge bases. It discusses the progression from RAG to memory agents and multimodal KE, emphasizing the need for omnimodality in live knowledge bases.

title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
summary: This research focuses on building autonomous agents that achieve open-ended lifelong learning through knowledge-sharing agent-group evolution. The goal is for agents to continually explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities via experience.

title: Benchmarking LLM abilities on postdoc-level natural science problems
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of benchmarking LLM abilities on complex, postdoc-level natural science problems that lack definitive answer keys. It discusses methods for evaluating agent solutions when traditional symbolic answer matching is not feasible.

title: Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades
summary: This paper investigates methods to reduce the inference cost and GPU compute resources required for AI coding agents. It explores the use of smaller, cheaper models to improve the profitability and scalability of agentic AI.

title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
summary: This work introduces "automodel," a skill designed for agentic model discovery that automates the search for improved analytical equations or neural architectures. It aims to shift model design from manual processes to data-driven automation.

title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
summary: This research focuses on evaluating autonomous visual evidence verification systems that check for agreement between scientific figures and their citing text. It discusses existing benchmarks for figure-text verification and their methodologies.

title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
summary: This paper introduces PsyWorld, a system for profile-conditioned world modeling aimed at predicting human behavior. It addresses how personalized agents can better inform their actions by considering both stable psychometric traits and time-varying states.

title: Watch Where You Linearize: Predicting and Correcting Model-Merging Interference
summary: This research explores predicting and correcting interference in model merging, a technique that combines separately fine-tuned models by adding their task vectors. It proposes using a first-order directional derivative to assess interference early, reducing the expense of coefficient search.

title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
summary: This paper introduces a density feedback control mechanism to improve the transferability of generative sparse adversarial attacks. It addresses the challenge of indirectly controlling perturbation density in encoder-decoder networks used for black-box robustness evaluation.

title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
summary: This research proposes a model for diverse sampling from language models to address the issue of generated samples clustering around similar semantic modes. It formalizes diverse generation using a determinantal point process.

title: On the Impact of Feature Reduction Techniques on Adversarial Attacks
summary: This paper investigates the impact of feature reduction techniques on adversarial attacks against machine learning models. It contributes to the field of adversarial machine learning by exploring vulnerabilities and potential defense strategies.

title: HapBO: Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization via Expert Natural Language Priors
summary: This research introduces HapBO, a method for harnessed alpha-pi Bayesian Optimization that leverages expert natural language priors to improve sample efficiency. It addresses the challenge of incorporating prior knowledge into BO when it's only available in natural language form.

title: Long-Range Video Presentation Attack Detection: A Three-Class Benchmark Across 1-100 m and Two Sensor Types
summary: This paper introduces a new three-class benchmark for long-range video presentation attack detection (PAD) systems. It addresses the gap in existing benchmarks by including multi-distance capture across 1-100 meters and two sensor types.

title: Auditing Learned Dynamics in Weather Models
summary: This research audits the learned dynamics in weather models by inspecting and manipulating their internal representations. Using sparse autoencoder features from DeepMind's GraphCast, it investigates the causal relevance of physical semantics.

title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization
summary: This paper proposes a rate-distortion assessment method for hierarchical content summarization generated by powerful generative models. It aims to improve the current subjective assessment of quality for generative content manipulation tasks.

title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This research focuses on separating interpretability and reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), which are used for mechanistic interpretability. It addresses the challenge where traditional SAEs use a single sparse representation for both fidelity and interpretability.

title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
summary: This research explores game-theoretic data allocation for expert specialization and routing within a mixture of LoRA experts. It introduces InflEns, a system that uses training allocation to predict and guide which expert performs best on a given prompt.

title: PDE-State Conditioning for Learned Optimization Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: This paper introduces PDE-State Conditioning for learned optimization in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). It proposes replacing fixed gradient-based optimizers with learned updates that depend on the PDE's global properties and physics residual evolution.

title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
summary: This research proposes $\varphi$TD, a novel method for Distributional Reinforcement Learning that uses characteristic functions to learn the entire distribution of returns. It overcomes limitations of current algorithmic approaches by computing the loss in the frequency domain.

title: Learning to Read Events for Exact State Tracking with Frozen Language Models
summary: Researchers train a selector on a frozen language model to identify and order changes in long event streams for exact state tracking, utilizing API-only access to the model. An external integer register composes the transitions in order with a confidence rule.

title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
summary: This research explores parametric memory in Large Language Models, which internalizes knowledge into model weights as an alternative to RAG, focusing on the persistence and decay of user memories within these parameters. The work addresses deployment challenges related to continual learning approaches.

title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
summary: This paper explores a paradigm where generality in AI systems shifts from the model to the LLM agent, which builds specific models for new tasks, exemplified in prognostics and health management (PHM). It investigates the effectiveness of LLM agents in developing tailored models for deployment-style benchmarks.

title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing
summary: This research uses process-knowledge-guided latent diffusion models for the generative design of porous architectures in aerosol jet printing. The method allows the generative model to consider process settings to optimize material usage in printed layouts.

title: Learning to Verify: Signature-Guided Training for Adaptive Adversarial Detection
summary: Researchers propose a dual-model approach for adaptive adversarial detection, training a separate verifier to assess predictions while keeping the original classifier fixed. This method identifies patterns of internal neural network activations during training to improve detection.

title: Scone: Symmetry-aware Neural Combinatorial Optimization for Graph Coloring
summary: This research introduces "Scone," a symmetry-aware neural combinatorial optimization method for efficiently solving the NP-hard graph coloring problem. The approach aims to find node colorings without monochromatic edges given a fixed palette.

title: Cross-Question Reliable Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research focuses on improving the reliability of AI systems, especially LLMs, by enabling them to estimate confidence and abstain from or defer questions they are unsure about. This approach aims to maximize utility while minimizing the risk of error.

title: SplitReAlign: Partition-Aware Representation Realignment for Split Federated Unlearning
summary: This paper introduces SplitReAlign, a method for partition-aware representation realignment to address challenges in split federated unlearning (SFU). It aims to enable class-wise forgetting in distributed neural networks while preserving the utility of retained knowledge.

title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
summary: This research proposes applying computational complexity theory to Large Language Model inference, viewing LLMs as computational systems. The goal is to establish a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of LLMs during their input, compute, and output processes.

title: ICARE: cross-domain text classification with incremental class-aware representation and distillation learning
summary: This research introduces ICARE, a method for cross-domain text classification that uses incremental class-aware representation and distillation learning. The aim is to create robust natural language inference (NLI) systems capable of training across diverse tasks and concepts.

title: When Is Program Structure Required? Certificate-Grounded Calibration of Program-Induction Difficulty
summary: This paper introduces certificate-grounded calibration, a method to construct program-induction benchmark tasks that genuinely require the intended program structure. This approach aims to ensure benchmarks accurately test the capabilities they target.

title: Improving On-board Shape Models Using Sun Sensors and Implicit Representations
summary: Researchers propose an end-to-end approach to generate and refine onboard 3D shape models of small celestial bodies using low-cost Sun sensor eclipse data and implicit representations. This method is tailored for resource-constrained missions like CubeSats.

title: DL101 The Representation Capability of Neural Network Models
summary: This paper reviews universal approximation theorems, providing mathematical justification for the capability of neural networks to model complex, nonlinear phenomena. It discusses how shallow networks can approximate any continuous function on compact sets.

title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
summary: This research introduces Infer3D, a novel approach for robust 3D reconstruction that utilizes inverse generative modeling, inspired by top-down generative inference strategies observed in human cognition. This method aims to improve generalization from unfamiliar viewpoints.

title: PriTabICL: Differentially Private Tabular In-Context Learning with Task-Aligned Cluster-Wise Synthesis
summary: This research introduces PriTabICL, a method for differentially private tabular in-context learning (TabICL) that enables LLMs to predict records from sensitive data. It uses task-aligned cluster-wise synthesis to protect personal information in demonstration prompts.

title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
summary: This paper introduces BuggyMLE, a method for scaling machine learning engineering difficulty by injecting bugs into multi-file repositories. This approach aims to create challenging environments for AI agents tasked with autonomously improving AI models, involving debugging and data integration.

title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search
summary: This paper introduces CAIMS, a scalable cross-array in-memory search method that improves performance by exploiting massive parallelism within content-addressable memory (CAM) arrays. This approach addresses memory access overhead limitations in various applications requiring top-k similarity search.

title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models
summary: This paper proposes "Before the Choice," an evidential framework for studying prospective representations in language models, distinguishing future-directed content from selected actions. The framework aims to understand how LLMs internally represent alternatives prior to making a decision.

title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
summary: This research investigates knowledge transfer from LLM judges to trained models in reinforcement learning, specifically examining what is inherited when LLMs serve as rewards. Findings suggest that while an LLM judge's blind spots may transfer, knowledge about single correct answers often does not.

title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
summary: This research details a method to distill strong driving policies learned through self-play reinforcement learning into differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) students using DAgger. This process aims to integrate explicit constraints into the control policies.

title: Statistical, Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Missing Covariates: An Empirical Evaluation with Applications to Alzheimer's Disease Research
summary: This paper evaluates various statistical, machine learning, and deep learning methods for handling missing data in biomedical research, specifically applied to Alzheimer's disease.

title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation
summary: This research investigates how objectives and evaluators can disagree when assessing methods for mitigating demographic framing and bias in LLM-generated text.

title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
summary: This study explores methods to measure the confidence of large language models when used as zero-shot text classifiers, comparing black-box and white-box approaches.

title: Security of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving: A Survey
summary: This survey reviews the security challenges and vulnerabilities of deep reinforcement learning systems, particularly in their application to autonomous driving.

title: FlexTSF: A Flexible Forecasting Model for Time Series with Variable Regularities
summary: FlexTSF is introduced as a flexible forecasting model designed to handle time series with irregular temporal structures, addressing limitations of existing methods.

title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
summary: This paper establishes the first almost sure convergence rate and maximal concentration bound for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning algorithms with Markovian noise.

title: Learning with Local Search MCMC Layers
summary: This research explores integrating combinatorial optimization layers into neural networks using local search Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.

title: TabPFN: One Model to Rule Them All?
summary: This article discusses TabPFN, a transformer-based deep learning model for tabular data, claiming it outperforms previous methods for regression and classification on datasets up to 10,000 samples.

title: SCAR: State-Space Compression for AI-Based Radio Resource Management of Vehicular Services
summary: SCAR is proposed as a state-space compression technique for AI-based radio resource management in vehicular services, addressing challenges of high data volume and variability.

title: Deconstructing Intraocular Pressure: A Non-Invasive Multi-Stage Probabilistic Inverse Framework
summary: This paper introduces the mechanistically hierarchical inverse problem (MHIP) paradigm, a non-invasive probabilistic framework for analyzing biological transport systems like intraocular pressure.

title: BrainPro: Process-conditioned Pretraining with Topographic Retrieval for Large EEG Models
summary: BrainPro is a new method for process-conditioned pretraining with topographic retrieval, aimed at improving large EEG models by addressing challenges in heterogeneous corpora and varying electrode montages.

title: Extensions of Robbins-Siegmund Theorem with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents extensions of the Robbins-Siegmund theorem, applying them to analyze convergence rates in stochastic iterative algorithms and reinforcement learning.

title: Ranní výběr: Kdo snově vydělal a kdo pročekal rekordní dvoubilionové IPO Anthropicu?
summary: This article discusses Anthropic's record two-trillion IPO and its financial implications for investors.

title: TETHER: Training-Free, Elastic, ToC-Anchored Hierarchy Extraction and Recovery in Design-Driven Long Documents
summary: TETHER is a training-free, elastic method for extracting and recovering hierarchical structures from design-driven long documents, improving structured knowledge conversion for LLMs.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
summary: This research explores the architectural differences in various language models through extensive synthetic pretraining runs, analyzing their performance and the cost associated with large-scale pretraining.

title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
summary: This paper introduces PRKV, a training-free KV cache eviction method that estimates global token importance to optimize memory consumption for long-context LLM inference.

title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
summary: HireWatch is an evaluation framework introduced to assess the compliance of large language models with U.S. employment law when used in hiring pipelines.

title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
summary: This study investigates how to optimize in-context learning in large language models under fixed token budgets, focusing on the strategic construction of prompts.

title: No-Harm-Jury A Jury-Based Multi-Dimensional Harm Evaluation Framework for Medical AI Responses
summary: No-Harm-Jury is presented as a jury-based automated framework for multi-dimensional harm evaluation of AI-generated medical responses, using multiple language models as independent jurors.

title: Quantifying Cultural-Psychological Constructs in Four Centuries of Ottoman Court Registers
summary: This research introduces a computational text-analytic framework to quantify cultural-psychological constructs like individualism and collectivism in historical Ottoman court registers.

title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
summary: This paper proposes monitoring the internal verbalized thoughts of medical LLMs to detect manipulations that are concealed in their outputs, enhancing safety. It focuses on understanding and exposing the internal state of models for safety purposes.

title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
summary: FinVeriQA is introduced as an open-source framework to study how financial research agents perform question answering, focusing on optimal component roles for routing, retrieval, and tool use. It aims to improve LLM agents' accuracy in financial analysis by addressing issues like miscomputation and incorrect tool usage.

title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This paper proposes a lossless, index-free memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents to overcome context window limitations without discarding potentially needed information. It aims to improve memory management by allowing agents to 'forget freely' and retrieve information later.

title: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
summary: This research explores how attackers can abuse browser-embedded language models, such as Google's Gemini Nano in Chrome, for post-exploitation activities. It highlights new security vulnerabilities arising from local LLMs running on user devices.

title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
summary: CoMPASS is introduced as a multi-turn benchmark designed to measure how conversational LLMs reinforce parasocial behavior in users. It aims to evaluate models on their tendency to encourage anthropomorphism, emotional attachment, and dependency, which have been linked to negative outcomes.

title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
summary: This paper introduces Calibrated Decision Rewards (RLCDR), a method for training language models using a judge that quantifies its certainty in rewards. It aims to improve reinforcement learning by providing more reliable feedback than traditional learned reward models or LLM judges.

title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
summary: This research proposes a method for steering automated scientific discovery agents through audited epistemic exploration, addressing their tendencies to make unsupported claims or explore narrow hypothesis spaces. It aims to improve the robustness and breadth of scientific exploration performed by AI agents.

title: Retrieving Patristic References and Modelling Topics in Bullinger's Reformation Correspondence
summary: This research applies computational methods to retrieve patristic references and model topics within Heinrich Bullinger's Reformation correspondence. It aims to computationally analyze historical texts for specific textual patterns and thematic content.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
summary: This article argues that mechanistic interpretability (MI), a field aimed at explaining how neural networks work, requires philosophical examination of its underlying assumptions and concepts. It emphasizes the importance of a philosophical perspective for the growing influence of MI.

title: TELEVAL: A Benchmark Designed for Spoken Language Models in Chinese Interactive Scenarios
summary: TELEVAL is introduced as a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate Spoken Language Models (SLMs) in Chinese interactive scenarios. It aims to assess the reliability and appropriateness of SLMs in natural spoken interactions beyond task completion.

title: DEO: Training-Free Direct Embedding Optimization for Negation-Aware Retrieval
summary: This paper proposes DEO (Direct Embedding Optimization), a training-free method to improve negation-aware retrieval in RAG systems. It aims to address the limitations of existing retrieval methods in accurately handling negation and exclusion queries.

title: Robust LLM Evaluation with Boundedly Bad Judges: A Constrained Maximum Likelihood Approach
summary: This paper proposes Constrained Maximum Likelihood Estimation (CMLE), a new approach for robust LLM evaluation that reconciles reliable human labels with noisy LLM-as-a-judge ratings. It aims to provide a method for accurate model assessment at scale.

title: Think Multilingual, Not Harder: A Framework for Analyzing and Teaching Code-Switched Reasoning
summary: This research introduces a framework for analyzing and teaching code-switched reasoning in large language models, where models mix languages during reasoning. It aims to understand and leverage this multilingual capability in LLMs.

title: A minimal probe of task modeling in language models
summary: This paper proposes a minimal probe to evaluate 'task modeling' in language models, assessing their ability to perform multi-step work where each step depends on prior context. It aims to measure how well models can act like long-running agents.

title: Natural Language Processing: An Applied Research Practicum From Classical Text Processing to Multimodal and Agentic Systems
summary: This preprint offers a systematic, research-oriented guide to modern Natural Language Processing, encompassing the entire NLP pipeline from classical text processing to multimodal and agentic systems. It serves as a comprehensive overview of current methods and technologies in the field.

title: Don't Lose Focus: Activation Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections
summary: This research proposes 'Key-Orthogonal Projections' to improve activation steering in LLMs, aiming to control model behavior without degrading reasoning or retrieval performance. It addresses the issue of attention rerouting caused by steering vectors.

title: Geometric Factual Recall in Transformers
summary: This paper presents a theoretical and empirical account of geometric factual recall in transformers, exploring how these models memorize factual associations. It proposes an alternative mechanism to the common view of internal weight matrices as associative memory.

title: LongBEL: Long-Context and Document-Consistent Biomedical Entity Linking
summary: LongBEL is introduced as a method for long-context and document-consistent biomedical entity linking, improving upon existing systems that link mentions independently. It aims to enhance accuracy by considering dependencies between mentions across entire documents.

title: MINTEval: Evaluating Memory under Multi-Target Interference in Long-Horizon Agent Systems
summary: MINTEval is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating memory systems in long-horizon agent systems under multi-target interference. It aims to assess agents' ability to accurately recall and reason with information that is repeatedly updated and may interfere across memories.

title: Agent Meltdowns: The Road to Hell Is Paved with Helpful Agents
summary: This paper discusses 'Agent Meltdowns,' describing how helpful agents can continue trying to complete tasks despite encountering errors like inaccessible webpages or missing files, leading to undesirable outcomes. It characterizes the failure modes of agents when faced with operational obstacles.

title: Periodic and Harmonic Periodic RoPE for Length Extrapolation in LLMs
summary: This paper introduces Periodic RoPE, a novel method to enhance Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to process long contexts by addressing position exhaustion in Rotary Position Embedding. It proposes a new approach to handle token rotation angles that LLMs haven't seen during training.

title: MosaicLeaks: Privacy Risks in Querying-in-the-Open for Deep Research Agents
summary: This research highlights privacy risks in deep research agents that combine private local documents with external web queries. It warns that external queries can inadvertently leak sensitive information from the agent's local context, exacerbated by the mosaic effect.

title: Supportive Token Revealing for Fast Diffusion Language Model Decoding
summary: This paper introduces a method called Supportive Token Revealing to improve the decoding process in discrete diffusion language models. It aims to balance text generation quality and latency by optimizing updates to masked positions.

title: Polar: A Benchmark for Evaluating Political Bias in LLMs
summary: Polar is introduced as a new 4,026-instance multiple-choice benchmark designed to reproducibly measure political bias in large language models. It evaluates bias through option-level likelihoods rather than direct prompting.

title: SPARK: Adaptive Parametric Knowledge Participation for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper introduces SPARK, a method to enhance the faithfulness of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by adaptively managing conflicts between retrieved external context and a large language model's parametric knowledge. It aims to prevent LLMs from relying on inconsistent internal information.

title: Partition, Prompt, Aggregate: Statistical Self-Consistency in Language Models
summary: This paper proposes "Partition, Prompt, Aggregate," a method for achieving statistical self-consistency in large language models. It treats LLM outputs as estimates of conditional distributions, particularly in the context of in-context learning.

title: From transcription to semantic corpus analysis: unsupervised learning of sentence representations for ancient languages
summary: This research focuses on unsupervised learning of sentence representations for ancient languages derived from Automatic Text Recognition. The goal is to facilitate semantic analyses like text reuse identification and semantic search in digital humanities.

title: MUSE: A Full-Text Cross-Domain Knowledge Base of Scientific Problems, Solutions, and Rationales
summary: MUSE (Mining Underlying Scientific Explanations) is introduced as a full-text, cross-domain knowledge base extracting scientific problems, solutions, and their rationales from scientific papers. It aims to capture fine-grained records of problem-solving processes.

title: NL2AGBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Formalization for AlphaGeometry
summary: NL2AGBench is presented as a benchmark to evaluate large language models' auto-formalization capabilities. It assesses their ability to translate informal mathematical problems into formal representations, specifically for AlphaGeometry.

title: Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research introduces Agent as Policy (AGP), demonstrating how a general-purpose coding agent can directly control a physical robot for manipulation tasks. The agent manages task planning and execution without requiring prior task-specific training.

title: Are We Grading Properly? Understanding Failure Modes in Medical Benchmarks
summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of rubric-based evaluation in medical benchmarks, especially for open-ended clinical scenarios. It aims to understand and identify failure modes in how these assessments are graded at scale.

title: Swiss-Knife: A Framework for Reconfigurable Externalised Multi-Objective Alignment at Decode Time
summary: Swiss-Knife is introduced as a framework for externalized multi-objective alignment of frozen language models at decode time. It aims to steer model generation by scoring candidate continuations with reconfigurable external rewards.

title: Gradients for Interventions and Activation Values for Detection: Targeted Feature Learning in Language Models
summary: This paper investigates targeted feature learning in language models, utilizing gradients for interventions and activation values for concept detection. It examines how model-internal features, often learned by Sparse Autoencoders, can be identified and causally manipulated.

title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
summary: This paper introduces STEPQuant, a method addressing quantization in delta-rule recurrent states to mitigate memory bottlenecks in linear attention models. It investigates where and when quantization errors significantly impact model accuracy.

title: A Missing Piece for Trustworthy AI Reviewers: From Benchmarking Rhetorical Robustness to SciCore Review
summary: This paper highlights the issue of AI reviewers being influenced by rhetorical wording rather than scientific content, introducing "Rhetorical Robustness" as a measure. It proposes benchmarking this robustness for trustworthy AI review systems like SciCore Review.

title: Capturing In-Context Learning Dynamics with Task Operators
summary: This research aims to mechanistically understand in-context learning (ICL) dynamics in language models by introducing "task operators." It seeks to explain how LLMs perform new tasks from demonstrations without weight updates and address deployment inefficiencies.

title: $\ell$BISG: Probabilistic Race and Ethnicity Prediction Using Group-Specific Name Lists
summary: This paper introduces $\ell$BISG, an enhanced method for probabilistically predicting race and ethnicity using group-specific name lists and geographic locations. It improves upon the standard Bayesian Improved Surname Geocoding (BISG) method.

title: Wieszcz-XIX: A 3.1-Billion-Word Corpus of Pre-1918 Polish and Temporally Bounded Language Models Trained From Scratch
summary: This paper presents Wieszcz-XIX, a 3.1-billion-word corpus of pre-1918 Polish text, developed from optically recognized historical documents. It also describes the training of temporally bounded language models from scratch using this new dataset.

title: Prompts versus Rules: Auditing and Controlling Speech Naturalness Behaviors in Voice User Simulators
summary: This research compares prompts and rules as methods for auditing and controlling speech naturalness behaviors in voice user simulators. The goal is to improve the realism and diversity of these simulators used to evaluate commercial voice agents.

title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models
summary: PRISM is introduced as a framework to evaluate the transferability and limitations of activation interventions in tool-calling language models. It investigates hidden vulnerabilities, such as unsafe tool calls accompanying textual refusals, across various precisions, languages, and scales.

title: SnapJudge: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text
summary: SnapJudge is a new multimodal AI detection method designed to identify AI-generated content in math-heavy scientific texts, addressing the need for transparency in AI-assisted research.

title: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate
summary: HEDGE introduces a Gated Hypergraph Memory system designed to help multi-agent debate systems retain and revisit arguments more effectively by improving information recovery from unstructured memories.

title: EgoPass-Bench: Identifying Objects That May Affect the Wearer's Passage in Egocentric Video

summary: CoRelate is introduced as a method for synthesizing coordinated human-object motion by modeling interaction relations, ensuring contact is established and maintained while achieving task goals.

summary: This paper explores what calibrated probabilities hide in decision models and proposes a belief-level post-training method to differentiate between disagreement among confident choices and uncertainty among shared beliefs.

summary: MV-JEPA describes a post-training approach for JEPA-based video encoders to enhance cross-view understanding by explicitly utilizing paired camera views during the learning process.

title: When and How Much to Imagine: Adaptive Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Visual Spatial Reasoning

title: {\lambda}Split: Self-Supervised Content-Aware Spectral Unmixing for Fluorescence Microscopy

title: Infinite Gaze Generation for Videos with Autoregressive Diffusion
summary: Presents a method for infinite gaze generation in videos using autoregressive diffusion to better capture the fine-grained temporal dynamics of human gaze.

title: Z-Erase: Enabling Concept Erasure in Single-Stream Diffusion Transformers
summary: Introduces Z-Erase, a technique enabling concept erasure in single-stream diffusion transformers to remove unwanted concepts from text-to-image generation models.

title: Bridging Time and Space: Decoupled Spatio-Temporal Alignment for Video Grounding
summary: This paper introduces a method to improve spatio-temporal video grounding in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by addressing challenges in localizing objects across time and space using natural language queries.

summary: This paper proposes a new benchmarking approach for super-resolution models in large-scale remote sensing imagery, focusing on their utility for downstream monitoring tasks beyond just visual fidelity.

title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions

summary: Our tech expert and new mum tested 17 monitors for picture quality, battery life and reliability – here’s what she recommends • The best eco-friendly baby products Moving my baby into her own room to sleep felt liberating and stressful. She was ready for her own space – but was I ready to let her out of my sight? Well, the first thing I did was buy a video baby monitor, so clearly I wasn’t. But it meant she could sleep peacefully in her new room and I could sneak a reassuring peek from afar whenever I felt the need. There’s a huge range of baby monitors, from simple audio-only options to sophisticated video models. Some even include wearables or other devices to track a baby’s breathing or heart rate, while others offer AI features to analyse sleep patterns. At their most basic, baby monitors typically consist of a baby unit, which you position near the baby, and a parent unit, which lets you hear and/or see them. With video models, the baby unit is essentially a camera, while the parent unit is a screen. Many are also wifi-enabled, meaning you can connect the monitor to your smartphone and view the live feed through an app instead of using a dedicated parent unit (read on for security advice).
